source: There was an oath I took. A pact perhaps. Yes...
But the hunger. How could I have known there’d be such hunger?
Please. Bring me the glow. The glimmer. The shine off their backs.
And I will open every door.
And I will open every door.
You Quiet Ones dug too deep. You asked too much of the world.
But there is no answer. No bottom. No atonement.
You struck down the Echo Knight. But are still here. Why?
Because you are the Echo Knight.
I heard him fall. The Knight, by your stroke. And later I heard him rise again.
You Quiet Ones were born for dying. But this pit steals away your true death.
What could remain but madness.
You have seen your champion, Quiet One. Your plague breaker. Was he beautiful?
Cyvion the Sayer’s Chosen. Trampler of the Dead. Warden of the Whispers. He who set the first stone in the Great Gate.
He is but a voice to me, from a throat long silenced. Still echoing off the stone.
You met one. I smell it on you. A shade. A remnant. A Once Was.
Eldric, the Broken Vow, dressed in the dead. The first to drink the blackened blood and bend it to his will.
He does not remember. Many here get lost. And then become lost. I remember for them... what I can.
Was I a Quiet One once? Was this a bargain I made? For what, I wonder...
So long since there was another. Perhaps that means we won. Or lost. Could it be both?
This is where I fit. One key, one lock, one purpose. What is yours?
So. The Quiet One will see itself reborn...
I wonder what it will become.
I will see you again, in the darkness.
The Pestilence. It's already among us, Cerim.
I knew with the Pestilence returned, it wouldn't be long before your kind did as well.
But I fear the plague has already crept within Sacrament’s walls.
Two days ago I offered a potent rune to a woman who said her husband was ill.
A small mercy, but I have not heard from them since, and I worry he was worse than she let on.
Please visit their home in Beggar’s Alley. You can find me at the marketplace after.
Please visit their home in Beggar’s Alley.
The plague knows we are weakest when alone. But we are not alone, Cerim, not even you.
Visit their home near Beggar’s Alley - the one with the red door - and put my fears to rest. Or confirm them.
Have you checked on the house in Beggar’s Alley? I worry for their safety. And ours.
So it was as I feared. Our stone walls mean nothing to the plague.
I… I didn’t even know their names. I never thought to ask.
I will look after the girl. We are, all of us, the children of those who survived.
And the rune, I see you have it now. They are potent things, yet fickle. Each carries its own blessing.
Runes can be bonded to your weapon, or to your being itself. But removing them carries its own cost.
We are all soldiers now, in the one true war. The one my mother and her mother and hers spoke of in whispers.
A door was opened a thousand years ago. Perhaps together we can close it.
She is quarrelsome. She has nightmares. And I do not know if she has the talent, nor the patience, to learn to enchant.
But still, the rise and fall of her chest when she sleeps…
She can stay. As long as she wishes.
They’ll be out soon…
They told me to wait out here. Is it supper time yet? I hope momma makes dumpling soup.
They gave me this. Said it would keep me safe.
You can take it back to Eleanor. I need to stay here. In case they wake up.
I have to stay here. Do you think they’ll wake up soon?
Eleanor cooks me dumpling soup. It’s not the same as my mother’s.
But that’s alright. It doesn’t have to be.
Do you think I’ll always remember the difference?
She says I need to control my bad dreams instead of let them control me. That even dreams can be weapons.
I like the sound of that.
Next to God's will, the stone is weak as clay.
See how it crumbles.
It has no strength, because it has no conviction.
Soon the mountain will follow. Deliverance is an avalanche.
Look out - someone’s coming!
I won’t go back!
Once in Sacrament, we pawn our armor and catch the first ship off this wretched isle.
That simple, eh?
Hard part’s already done.
You do not belong here, Unspoken.
Nor do you deserve to bear witness to the fall of the Heretic’s Gate.
It is but a relic, dead on its feet. Like you.
Bainbridge was unworthy of God’s Embrace.
A quality perhaps you both share.
The pass is shut.
Entry to the pass is barred on order of the Madrigal.
The many-eyed God. The Dasha’s pagan four. Whatever it is you worship, Cerim - the Sayer I think it’s called?
All the same. Grown men playing make believe.
The god I worship spans a half million leagues and two hundred islands. She’s called empire.
No glory but the might of men, and all monuments in her name.
Move along.  For your own safety.
Haven’t you heard? The Gate’s comin’ down. Best stay clear.
No outsiders permitted.
Are you deaf? No entry til the holy city’s been freed from the stone.
Lift’s for official use only. If you wanna pass, speak with Primus Bainbridge.
Take it up with Bainbridge, not me.
Bainbridge himself came down to secure the area. And to track down deserters.
Don’t matter if you want in or want out - no one’s slipping his net.
I’m a man of faith! Put copper in every one of God’s palms, and not just on my son’s naming day.
But the Inquisition - I’m not sure I see my faith in them.
I suppose if God has hands, he has claws. If he has eyes, he has teeth.
Make the hair stand up on my neck, they do. I’ll be glad to be back on the mainland soon.
Inquisition serves the Church. Church serves the King. King serves God.
And somehow I end up working for all of ‘em.
Whatever I pictured when I was crowned a knight of House Bolein - it wasn’t this.
I’m no deserter. If there’s work to be done, I’ll see it through.
But... I understand. Backwater job like this, far from home, farmed out to the Inquisition.
Up to our ankles in shit, scratching at a big door. Know what’s on the other side? More shit.
Not one to complain, myself, of course. Just... sympathetic to the grievances of others.
We knights parade about in our armor, flashing the broadsword in our scabbard, but have you seen the Madrigal?
That’s real power. She’s got King Magnus's ear, and God has hers.
The weak always speak the loudest. While those in charge need barely whisper.
Magnus's Bolein army is more than 10,000 strong. But what’s that against the word of God.
Well they’ve done it. They’ve finally done it.
Survived floods and fires, foul abominations, not to mention the fickle winds of commerce. But Orvyn can only take so much.
Phalen’s “finest” have blocked the few roads that remain, save the lift just north of here.
And that damn pounding - can’t sleep, can’t eat without jangling my teeth. Shakes my turnips right out of the ground!
Next time you’re here, stranger, I surely won’t be.
What’s that dwindling speck, sailing away on the horizon? It’s Orvyn.
I am pleased to hear of the deserters' fate. I will inform the Madrigal.
Curse your God. The fire awaits us both.
In time, yes.
The many hands.
The eye within.
We serve at her pleasure. I can assure you that any others will meet the same end.
No. We will not tolerate any more doubt within your ranks, Primus. Not while we knock on salvation’s door.
Discipline takes time. It’s earned, not bought.
The Born God disagrees. Discipline is forged. It is a tool, molded in flame...
I... It will not happen again. I assure you.
...and sometimes, an effigy is needed. The weakness must burn, so the rest will kneel.
Speaker. The sigil of House Bolein is the phoenix. Born of flame...
You cannot burn what was born in the ashes... Please! I am a servant of the king!
So justice caught up with the deserters? Hmm, fair enough. Saves me the trouble.
I’ll have my men strip the uniforms from those dogs. All cowards deserve to meet their maker naked.
And I’ll inform the Inquisition that my ranks have been sewn up tight.
Consider my gaze averted.
You can hear it, can’t you? Feel it in your feet as well. And not a moment too soon if you ask me.
None may pass. Not even your kind, Cerim. The Madrigal’s “divine work” must not be disturbed.
Although...
I confess, some of my men proved to be anything but. Fled rather than see their duty through. A stain on the Bolein sigil.
Now I’ve the Inquisition breathing down my neck, going on about heresy and devotion.
I lost their trail in the caves to the west. Punish their cowardice and I might... step away from my post?
Just to notify our friends in red, of course.
We’ve lingered too long already on this backwater. My men grow hungry, sick, tired of stone.
Not the Inquisitors though. They seem to thrive off it. Whispering prayers around the firepit’s flames, cherishing their own suffering.
Answer me this: if everyone’s a martyr, then who’s left to get anything done?
Mercy is a virtue. Or so I’m told. But there can be no leniency for abandoning one’s duty.
Can you not hear them...
I can. The voices of the city.
The cobbler in Tannis Square, setting up for the morning market. And the clerics, singing at Morrow Hall.
The weaver humming to her loom. The horses, in the stables where I...
They’re gone. All of them.
The Vestals would always say the grace of God is like the sun on your face.
There was a moment, this brief moment, when I thought... I really thought...
But no. I don’t know where I’m meant to be if not right here.
Leave me, Cerim. Before my Keepers send you to the next life.
You again? Don’t linger too long, or it might be your head and my job.
Have a nice chat with the traitor?

Ah! That’s the one. 
...Now make it quick.
I don’t know what to tell you. The old spinning wheel ain’t what it used to be.
If I only had a few coppers, I might be able to let you in.
The prisoner is to be kept in the War Room until the Governor returns.
I would allow you in to interrogate her...
But I've so many keys with me. I can’t seem to remember which one opens this door.
Huh. Maybe a few coppers would spur my memory.
They’re stronger than you know, Cerim. Stronger even than they know.
When I first came to Sacra, I was told it was a godless, uncivilized place.
Instead I found a people full of grace and resilience - both qualities sorely lacking in Phalen.
I found... something else here too. If only for a time.
If you need me, you can find me in the War Room. But I pray you will not need me.
I come here at times, Cerim, for a moment of peace. Or what passes for peace of late.
There’s much to do. I need to send envoys to Tir and Havenport, warn them of the Gate’s breach.
I need to double the men on the ramparts. Check the reserves of grain, of swords and pikes, of medicine.
I need to... find my daughter.
A man once told me that we don’t learn to fight for what we love, we learn we love it because we fight.
Of course then he tried to ram a sword through my back.
Still, good advice is good advice.
Fifty men on the wall, and I’d trade them all for one more Cerim.
I’m glad you made it back through the Nameless Pass unscathed.
When the plague arrived, I tried to free the prisoners working in the quarry.
They were criminals, yes, but none of their crimes merited such punishment.
Those that weren’t monsters already became them.
I saved as many as I could. But it’s never enough, is it?
I know the Madrigal’s arrival means an ally in the fight against the plague.
But then why does my hand linger on my hilt?
Cerim. I came here for some solitude to collect myself.
And instead I received a most... troubling letter from one of the Watcher’s crows.
It seems a governor’s duties involve walking into the lion’s mouth over and over.
Not so different from a father’s duty.
Odessa can’t wait forever.
At times I envy the... cleanliness of your justice. Find the sickness. Cut it out.
Still, many visitors to Sacra end up tangled in her affairs and stay longer than intended.
Mine was a nine day visit. Twenty eight years ago.
The hunters were stocking food for The Rites of the Fallen. It’s an important tradition. A gathering, to honor those we’ve lost.
Too damn many lately.
The last time I saw Harol, he told me I was a traitor to both my blood and my God.
I thought Sacra was far enough from the throne to put all that behind. Maybe I was wrong.
Cerim. I’m glad to see you still standing. I thank you again for helping to... dispose of that poor wretch in the forest.
There was a time when I would have fought alongside you. But, these days, I’m afraid my sword rusts in its sheath.
Baurus’s warning. The Inquisition. The coming Rites. And all I can think of is Reed and his daughter.
If he finds the creature’s remains, do you think he’ll even recognize her? I hope not.
No man should live to see his child lost.
Sometimes I see the worst of myself in Odessa, and the best of... Nevermind.
I wonder if I may come to envy you, Cerim. No home, no family. Perhaps you have no fear as well?
...No. No, I think you do understand fear.
This clamor of shouts and cries from outside keeps interrupting my focus.
Has something happened? Nevermind, I don’t want to know.
Anything worth happening has already happened.
If the present mattered as much as the past, someone would’ve carved it in stone.
Sometimes I tell myself that all of history is a wave. Crests and troughs. Rise and fall.
But where are we upon it? On the rise, or on the fall?
They look to me, Cerim. For answers, for solace, for hope.
I can’t see the future. I can hardly see the herbs in my own garden.
Still I know that Marin will weather any storm. I may be old, but hope is older still.
What do I do, when the skies are clear and the breeze is warm?
I make tea.
And when the darkness spreads and the air smells of blood and death seems all but certain?
I make tea.
We Dasha survived the plague a thousand years ago. And we will again.
You have come far, warrior. And yet you have much farther to go.
I’m always glad to see you again, Cerim. You carry hope in your wake.
Marin’s doors are always open to you, Cerim. Even in dark times. Especially in dark times.
I don’t suppose you’ve done much gardening, have you, Cerim.
There’s a moment... just before a seedling pokes its leaves above the earth.
When all you can see is dry, barren dirt. A wasteland.
But life is there. Waiting to emerge.
I never thought I could learn from a seedling.
The Cerim again. That’s interesting...
Batee han lavasha bath’el. May you always be hungry, and always be fed.
Listen. Do you hear the voices?
The true ones. Of our village. Those silenced before.
I hear Cyriel, peddling his wares. And Francis, grumbling about his garden. And Greta, her pride in our ways.
We are healing, Cerim. Each of us.
You seem to have made this island your home.
If that’s true, I hope you’ll join us in Sacrament for the Rites of the Fallen.
It’s a... moment of grace, for all of Sacra.
Ellsworth may be a fool, but he’s a noble fool, may the Seeker protect him.
Ah, look who it is!
You're the talk of the town, you know. I think my father is a touch jealous.
Me? Of course not. The Cerim and I are fellow hunters. Kindred spirits!
A kindred spirit you nearly confused with a brigand in the Glades. Your eyesight -
- Was plenty sharp enough to fell an elk across the river!
It was really more of a creek.
Betrayed by my own flesh and blood. I’ll feed you to the next wolf I see.
Oh so I’m safe then.
Well, enjoy Sacrament, Cerim. We're headed for the Lowland Meadows soon, to rejoin the rest of our hunting party.
We'll be hunting for the Rites of the Fallen. It's a ceremony to honor those we've lost.
I'm not sure the Cerim care about our affairs.
They will once we return to Sacrament pulling a wagon piled high with meat and pelts.
Such spirit - I wonder where she gets it.
I hope we see you soon. Maybe next time you can teach me something?
Anything worth learning, you can learn from me.
I was right, wasn’t I?
Winnick won’t meet my eye. He only does that when I’m right.
So... Darak’s gone. A rough end, to rot down there in the dark, even for him.
All those poor souls he convinced to join him. Giving their lives for what? To burn Sacrament to the ground?
That’s not the way. Any more than groveling under the mainland’s yoke. Why can’t they see?
I hear the passing guards remark “Sacrament endures.” By the skin of her teeth, eh?
I’ve noticed the blacksmith’s apprentice Will keeps lingering around my cell.
Do me a favor and tell him I’m alright. And if that doesn’t work, tell him I don’t want to see him.
Whatever keeps him distant. It’s better that way.
Please, go. I will await my judgment, and you do... whatever it is you came here to do.
We all walk our own path. Even if mine is just circles around this damn cell.
Cerim! Look what the tide washed in. I didn’t think you survived.
Seems our fortunes have changed since we last spoke.
I’m afraid we might have to postpone our fight.
But if I’m spared the gallows, perhaps we can finish what we started.
Although judgment might take awhile.
My father would rather play servant to the Madrigal than speak with me.
It could be worse. We could be at the bottom of the sea.
I wish I could see the Madrigal’s face as she looks upon the Mountain Gate.
Maybe she can pray her way through a thousand years of stone.
I never imagined I would say this, but...
I’m glad our paths have crossed.
You should know, I - I had no idea there were Cerim on that ship. Not that it would’ve stopped me.
We attacked for good reason. Lives were lost, but far more would’ve died if it made landfall.
Let’s call it water under the bridge. And over the deck.
If it’s another bowl of porridge, I’ll take the gallows instead, thank you.
Oh, you. Alive and well I see. And it looks as though you’ve been to the Pass.
I wish I could’ve seen the Madrigal’s face when she saw the Mountain Gate shut.
Maybe she can pray her way through a thousand years of stone.
Your weapon looks like it saw use in the quarry. You should take it to the blacksmith for repairs.
If you do, there’s a boy there. His apprentice, Will. Tell him I’m alright. And that I’m...
Nevermind. Don’t trouble him.
You shouldn’t help them, Cerim, even if their cause seems to be your own.
You can’t serve the lesser of two evils without being lesser yourself.
No one really knows what they’re fighting for. But at least the Risen know what we’re fighting against.
Ugh. When did I become so dry? I sound like my father.
Forgive my lecturing. Talk is meaningless.
...A truth you seem to have taken to heart.
You walk your path, I’ll walk mine.
Even if mine is just circles around this damn room.
The Inquisition blames the Dasha for bringing back the Pestilence. Funny how the strong always fear the weak.
Cerim! How did you get in here?
Come to finish what we started? It might be a fair fight with me in chains!
You’re a strange one, Cerim. You talk when you should fight. Fight when you should run.
A word of advice - the people here don’t like those they don’t understand. Trust me.
If you’re looking for my father, he left with the vanguard. They’ll be at the Mountain Gate by now.
As a child I used to think he was so tall. But how could he be, when he's always kneeling before Phalen?
Bring him back and I might get these shackles off.
And then maybe we’ll finish our fight.
If you head through the quarry to the Mountain Gate, keep your eyes open.
See just what type of protection Sacrament provides its own.
I don’t know why you would come to a place like this, Cerim. Where the dead outnumber the living.
Expecting some kind of thanks?
I tried cutting Lara free from what was left of that thing, but...
It wouldn't let her go, even in death.
So I burned the lot of 'em.
I know it's a sin, but I'll be damned if my Lara rests forever coiled in the teeth of that beast.
These meadows are full of the Torn. And I'll put every last one of them down until I fall myself.
She died afraid. But worse, she died alone. Least I can do is the same.
Leave me be, Cerim. There's nothing for me back in Sacrament.
Should you find any more ichor, bring it here. Something still stirs within the Watcher.
The work, it... gives him focus. I think your triumphs are d - d - d - drawing him back into the world.
And who knows - perhaps my pestering plays its own role in his revival!
I hear you were venturing in the Black Trench. I had no idea you were a fellow enthusiast of all things septic!
I have some fascinating scrolls on the ideal material and orientation of sewer pipes. I’ll be sure to share them.
I hear you encountered the Balak Taw. Some say theirs is a robust and misunderstood culture of avian rituals and communion with the natural world.
Others say they’re just madmen who dress up like birds.
What did the Madrigal want with you at the Mountain Gate? Was there any news from Caylen?
The stories we heard out of Caylen were bad. The silence is worse.
It seems our small rookery is thick with the wayward. The Watcher hails from Caylen. I’m from Tir myself. And you... well, I don’t know.
I hear you came across a Savor lab in the Lowland Meadows. Dreadful stuff.
It’s been spreading all over the realm of late. Offering moments of bliss and then years of misery.
I once obtained a sample - for purely scientific reasons, I promise - but even I wasn’t able to extract its secrets.
On my way through the town square, I overheard two guards saying Odessa was to be summoned from her cell.
I lingered briefly to discern more - oh curiosity, that cruel vice! - but I could hear nothing over the din of some yapping mutt.
Some of Sacrament’s strays can be quite... insistent, wouldn’t you say?
I know our worldly affairs aren’t your - I mean you have much to do but... did Elsa seem troubled to you?
The Watcher told me: answers come to those who seek them.
Back when he... could say such things.
But maybe the answers she found weren’t the ones she wanted.
I can’t promise the Watcher will help again. His wisdom is vast, but his mind is… well, it's like a ransacked library.
Many things on Sacra are not as they once were, I suppose. I can’t recall ever seeing the Inquisition inside our walls!
Ellsworth’s left for the Mountain Gate already with the Madrigal - but have no fear, Sacrament is in good hands under Baron Winnick.
Oh! And I hear Elsa the historian is asking after you. She’s a... curious one. Most curious.
Whatever course you chart, be careful. This island crawls with villainy. I suggest you visit the market for supplies, before you leave the city.
Will, the blacksmith’s apprentice, seems to be kicking up quite a quarrel with Captain Randolph near the marketplace.
I imagine the boy would have more success arguing with a stone wall.
Oh - God’s reach, have you heard?
Ellsworth has returned from the Mountain Gate. They say people are gathering to meet him in the square. You should hurry!
Please keep seeking out the Torn, Cerim. And bring their blood back to the Watcher.
If only you could have seen him at his height, Cerim.
When the plague spread and his letters went unanswered, he fell into shadow.
But now... I can see light breaking on his face.
You extinguish the plague where you can. Summon more if you must. You defeat it and yet... you thrive off it.
Power and poison. Poison and power.
There is a frightening symmetry to it all.
Forgive my impertinence but... you won’t forget why you came to our isle, will you Cerim?
As long as you bring him the necessary materials, I believe the Watcher will craft what he can. How you use it, we leave in your hands.
Have you seen Speaker Lucian and his envoy just over the bridge? Or I think it’s Speaker Lucian. Hard to tell those Inquisitors apart.
I saw Baron Winnick speaking with Odessa in her cell by the cages. She may be Risen now, but they have much history.
Elsa the historian adores all things Cerim. I think she wishes she had been born a thousand years ago. She must be thrilled you’ve arrived.
The stones and timber abandoned in the quarry will not be wasted. Nor the labor of these fallen men and women.
All of us - put to use.
And you, Cerim? I hope your humiliation has not broken your spirit.
My faithful say you scurry to and fro over the island.
Don’t be surprised. God’s many eyes keep watch on everyone. Why shouldn’t we?
Tell me, Cerim - are you the last of your kind?
Sometimes I feel as though I’m the first of mine.
I’m surrounded by believers, yes, but they were born believing.
They didn’t look for it in the sewers and stables. In loss. In pain.
The last time I saw my old mentor, he said - he shouted, really - that I was lost to faith and flame.
I wonder if he waits for me. Beyond the Gate.
Both God and King called upon me to reclaim this island. Either alone would be enough. But together... I cannot fail.
At first I named the rookery crows after scholars. Then saints. Then, when I ran out of those, just letters, numbers.
I wonder which message found you. The hundredth? The thousandth?
If only it had been the first.
Time. I wish I had more time. Or less.
It’s the Cerim! Here, over here!
Is it really true - you killed the creature at the gate?
A Cerim in Sacrament. At my smithy no less! Well, Fillmore’s smithy. I’m just his apprentice Will.
Wait, Fillmore! On your way to Sacrament, did you encounter a blacksmith?
He went out beyond the wall and hasn’t come back. I hope he’s alright.
Oh, thank you. That’s a weight off my mind. Not quite ready to man the forge on my own.
I expect he’ll be back soon now that you’ve cleared the way.
And likely telling me that he cleared the way for you.
Hrassa twen. That’s Dasha for welcome, and safe travels.
I shouldn’t keep you - I’d venture you’re on your way to the rookery up above.
I heard about what happened at the gate.
Fillmore says a smith with eyes anywhere but down at his anvil is a smith with flattened fingers.
But he ain’t got family in Marin Village. And I don’t think he cares much for Odessa either.
I wish the whole of the island could fit behind Sacrament’s walls.
Let’s share a promise, Cerim. I’ll keep your blade sharp, and you keep our people safe. You swear it?
It’s a real honor to service your blade, Cerim.
And there’s no better blacksmith than Fillmore. He comes from a long line of ‘em.
Not me. Mine’s farmers all the way back!
But the first time I saw a hammer hitting steel, it was like it was singing for only me.
Fillmore can tell the coke in the forge is ready by color alone.
Me, I have to tell by how close I can stand to it!
Then you temper and quench, temper and quench, while you work it with the anvil.
I prefer a double piked anvil myself, with a low arch. What’s your favorite type of anvil?
Odessa was the one who introduced me to Fillmore. Since she was always going back and forth between Marin and here.
She’d walk me through the woods. We’d pick berries and mullseeds on the way.
I was just little then of course. I can walk myself now.
Not that I minded walking with her.
You know Fillmore’s content with his stall right here, but I’ve got bigger plans.
I’m gonna open a smithy in Tir. Another in Havenport.
I’ll train all my smiths personally though. So you always know you’re getting good work.
I’ve already picked out a name. But I can’t tell you. You might steal it!
I... I don’t know what to say.
Thank you might be a start, boy.
Cerim, thank you. I'm so glad the rest are safe.
Odessa, Irmgard, my parents. All of them.
Alright, enough blabbering on. Back to the forge.
But thank you, Cerim.
Did you reach Marin Village? Is everyone alright?
Focus on the work, boy. Don’t respect the forge for even a moment and she’ll take your hand.
But how can I find peace when they might be in danger?
Trust me, the work is the peace.
Please, Cerim, bring back news as soon as you’re able.
Stirring words. If only words were enough.
But don’t worry, Cerim - the blade on his hip is no ornament.
When the time comes for him to draw it... pray you’re at his back and not in his sights.
“The strength of our will” - a lovely sentiment... Think the crowd bought it?
I see it troubles you, what happened down below. Don’t give it another thought, friend.
Darak was never going to stop. His quarrel with Ellsworth was always personal. He had to be put down.
And we had to learn if we could trust each other. When you find that out, let me know will you?
As for Odessa, I suppose she was telling the truth. Don’t know what to make of that. Better for Ellsworth to decide.
Look at them go about their business. No word of thanks, no debt of gratitude.
No idea of the massacre averted just beneath their feet.
Hm. As it should be.
I swear, most days Sacrament’s a peaceful place. Then again, if this was most days, you wouldn’t be here.
Risen at our gates, the Pestilence lapping at our heels, and now a dead king. I guess there’s only one question left:
Why aren’t we all in the tavern? Ha! No man deserves to face the end of the world sober.
Never any love lost between Ellsworth and King Harol, mind you. But blood’s blood.
People think he’s made of stone. But I’ve known Ellsworth half my life and believe me – it weighs on him. All of it.
Well, go on, enjoy Sacrament’s delights. She’s a bit rough and tumble, but that’s how I like her.
A far cry from where I was raised. Frigid, in more ways than one.
Nasty business with that beast in the woods earlier.
You brought a piece of mercy to what was left of that poor girl. Now I just worry about the father.
Dangerous to take away a man’s whole world. Just ask Darak.
No one’s born a killer. Except maybe you.
While you’re here, there’s something I’ve been wanting to ask. And be honest...

Do you think I’d make a good Cerim? 
Ha Ha! Of course I would.
I’ve known Odessa since she was just a baby in Annora’s arms.
And still, the number of guards who say to my face that she should hang...
Makes me wonder what they say about her behind my back.
One more pint, then back to the gate. To the gallows. To the sewers and ramparts.
There’s a man in town, Horus, calls himself the official Shit Scraper.
Should I tell him I’ve already filled the position?
The Rites of the Fallen can’t come soon enough if you ask me... This city’s like a thread pulled too taut.
Eyes on the sky, Cerim.
First Darak below our feet, now demons in the air. Why did we even build these walls?
My scouts say the Pestilence is boiling over the land faster than ever before.
As if I’m a blind man. They might as well tell me the sun’s in the sky.
We don’t have enough men to hold down the city, let alone push beyond the gates.
You’re on your own out there Cerim.
You have my thanks and best wishes. That and two copper will buy you a pint.
A word of advice? Fight dirty. Drown them, burn them, stab them in the back.
Survival is its own honor.
WINNICK: Impressive. This isn’t a sewer anymore, it’s a tomb.
RATTIGAN: See, I knew it! Sacrament stands because of me.

WINNICK: It wasn’t your place, Cerim, to make a deal with a prisoner. 
Nor, perhaps, my place to let you.
WINNICK: But don’t worry, he was never out of our sight.
RATTIGAN: Tell them, Cerim, I honored our deal. And a hero deserves a hero’s pardon!

WINNICK: Sacrament doesn’t bargain with murderers. You’re headed for 
hard labor at the Mountain Gate. By order of the Madrigal.
RATTIGAN: You shit-smiling bastard!

WINNICK: And you... Well, I think we understand each other, Cerim. 
You and I, we do what needs to be done.
Cerim, listen, please, you and I, we’ve grown close haven’t we? Over the course of our little adventure. Maybe even friends?
I’m trying to live by the straight and narrow. To make amends.
But these brutes, they can’t see beyond a man’s past!
Well we’ll see how high and mighty you are with a knife in your throat!
I won’t forget this, Cerim. I won’t forget you.
You wanted to know which promises I keep. I’ll tell you - this one.
I don’t think I’ll be telling Ellsworth you released that rat from his cage.
But I won’t be telling him my role in all this either.
I think we understand each other, Cerim. You and I, we...
...We do what needs to be done.
You’d be harsh on this marauder too if you saw what he did to two of my guards in their sleep.
Not a trace of honor on his breath.
Come back to me! I’ll keep you safe! I will... I’ll keep you safe...
You belong to me, Annora! By my side! Don’t go... Don’t leave me...
Marin. We can still go back to Marin. It’s not too late...!
His blood isn’t royal. It’s... It’s poison! Yes! Poison...
No! You can’t have her!
Thank you kindly. Now what was it I promised in return? Hehe, ah, yes.
The problem with you holier-than-thou types is you never look down. It’s the sewers! Miles and miles of ‘em under your feet.
The Risen in the outskirts are just a diversion. Darak’s men are gonna pour into Sacrament like stinking shit.
I’ll slip out when the guards rotate. Meet me at the sewer drain. Down on the coast. Maybe you still have time to stop them. Maybe not.
What, don’t think I’ll be there? I’m a man of my word! Or at least some of them.
It ain't fair. We didn't do nothing wrong.
Cerim! Maybe you can help clear our name. Tell him what happened, Learl.
We got demoted by that bastard Winnick just because one prisoner - one! - slipped his cage.
I mean losing one out of... however many - them's good odds!
We didn't even have the key! That was that drunk oaf Gerard. But where's he?
If you ain't someone's nephew or cousin, they just toss you out with the trash.
Well, I am Captain Randolph's cousin. That's how I got the job. But that's really a technicality.
With our luck they'll have us guarding latrines next. And then blame us when they smell like shit.
Eh, long as it's inside the walls and not atop 'em, I won't complain. Least not too much.
I can't for the life of me figure out how that bugger slipped free.
We deserve answers.
Your duty is to Sacrament.
We look to you, not the Cerim, for protection.
What's Ellsworth's plan? What steps are you taking to keep us safe? How will you defend the city?
Fair questions, all of them. Deserving of answers.
Answers, I'm afraid, we're unable to provide. Above our station, you see.
With winged demons in the air and plague outbreaks afoot, it's easy to forget we have other duties.
Some stand guard atop the wall. While others guard against petty theft. Or poaching. Or vagrancy.
Different responsibilities. But equal.
I don't need your help, Cerim. Nothing good can come from meddling in unnatural forces.
A wise observation.
If anyone is to stand up to these monsters in the sky, it's Sacrament's own guard.
Although we shouldn't be too quick to judgment.
All tools have their uses.
You swore an oath to defend the city of Sacrament.
An oath we would never break.
Not without good reason.
If it's Darak you seek, make your way through the underground passage.
But do not trust a rustling bush. The Risen are everywhere.
On guard, Conrad! Someone approaches.
The Cerim! About bloody time.
Indeed.
Are you hunting the Torn, or chasing human prey?
We're on the trail of a warlord called Darak. Winnick's orders.
We've searched the Lowland Meadows to the south, but the Risen have deserted the area.
The only place left to go is north... through that cave there.
We just thought we'd take a moment here first.
We're not delaying. Simply... resting.
Replenishing.
It's important to be well-nourished before battle.
Good luck, Cerim. We'll... be right behind you.

Listen. This is all a mistake. I took these clothes off a corpse on the coast. 
Being cold isn’t a crime is it? I’m no Risen.

Okay, I am Risen. But I’m a father too. You got children? I’ve got three myself, 
probably at home right now worried sick. Have a heart and let me free.
Fine, no kids. But I’ve got copper! Stashed away. Let me go and I’ll lead you straight to it.
And whatever they say I did, I swear I’ll never do it again. Not that I did it in the first place.
Oh, sniffing about for the governor’s daughter? Who’s side is she on anyway?
Not that it matters - she’s right, you know. The real attack is yet to come. Darak’s moving on the city itself.
But there may still be time to stop him. Darak left me to die. Least I can do is return the favor.
Tell me, friend, do you want to be a hero? Course you do, everyone does.
Spring me from this cage, and I’ll make you Sacrament’s savior.
These guards couldn’t keep a snail locked up in its own shell. You poke around, you’ll find the key.
Those guards won’t look twice at you. You’re a “guest of the city”...
Not another word from me until there’s no iron between us.
I’m reformed, I am. Ashamed and repentant. You should tell the guards - no need to punish a man who already punishes himself.
Talked to the other prisoners, did you? Don’t judge me for the company I keep. Revolution makes strange bedfellows.
Take us for example.
But I hope you learned something of value, Cerim.
All I’ve learned is that the porridge they serve the prisoners might be worse than the gallows.
I’m not... afraid of dying. But that doesn’t mean I want to.
You again. Gods, I’d rather sing in the town square than say this but... Maybe you can help me.
Darak’s always harbored a deep hatred of my father.
I never imagined he could move against Sacrament itself, but... He wouldn’t share his schemes with me.
The people here may be blind or broken, under the mainland’s boot for so long they mistake it for protection.
But that doesn’t mean they deserve to die.
Winnick said his men captured some of Darak’s faithful after the battle.
You should see if any of them can tell you more.
One of the other prisoners here might be able to help you.
I must sound like a fool. Most of Sacrament wants me hung, and here I am worrying about their tomorrow.
I imagine you know a thing or two about thankless tasks.
You don’t understand!
Darak’s a mad dog, but he’s no fool. Why would he draw your men to Orban Glades and then flee?
Because he was defeated, that’s why. If he returns, our stone walls will be there to greet him.
And why should I trust anything you have to say about the Risen?
Some of us join the Risen to build a better world. And some just to tear down the old one.
And some give speeches from behind bars.
Let me tell you a story, Cerim, if you’ve come to keep me company.
Because that’s what friends are for.
So there’s two fish swimming in the sea, right? And one says to the other, I’m hungry.
And the other, he wants to be a pal, so he goes looking. And when he comes back he says there’s some tasty–looking moss in that cave over there.
So the first fish goes in the cave, eats the moss, but says he’s still hungry.
So his friend finds him another cave. Says there’s some little white crawlies inside.
The first fish goes in, eats the worms, says he’s still hungry.
So his friend finds him one last cave. Says it’s right over there. And the first fish swims in.
But this cave’s got an eel in it.
And the eel gobbles the fish right up. And the other fish says - there, now you’re not hungry. Not anymore.
Maybe there’s a world where you and I make things right. But it’s not this one.
Look everyone - it’s the Cerim. The Cerim have come. To save us.
Don’t worry, I’ve been in holes deeper and cages smaller than this.
Aren’t bars tight enough that I can’t wriggle out of them.
And when I do, you and I will have a nice long talk. Or a very short one.
Guard! This Cerim here’s interrupting my work!
That turnip has the damn <color=#f29819>keys</color> with him.

Where’s that miserable runt wandered off to? He’s supposed to 
relieve me, I’ve got a date with Elga tonight.
Who, Gerard? He was dripping pissed, I told him to go dunk his head in the <color=#f29819>fountain</color>.

Well, that’s all right for some people, getting drunk on the job. 
But that turnip has the damn <color=#f29819>keys</color> with him.

Looks like you’re stuck with me. Why don’t you invite ol’ Elga 
to come round here? We can both enjoy her company.
Sod off.
Please...
Help me... Please...
Shoulda never come down here, never listened to Darak. You gotta believe me, I didn’t throw in with the Risen to burn down Sacrament. And not to... to...
Please, kill me. I don’t wanna end up like them...
Mother, Maker, Seeker, Forsaken, please watch over me…
Talo, it's me! Don't you recognize me?
WAIT!
I wouldn’t waste your time with those prisoners. Unless it’s to gloat before they swing.
I don’t know how many more are out there, but at least those worms are where they belong.
As for Odessa, well, she’ll await Ellsworth's judgment along with the rest of them.
You’ve proven yourself an ally of Sacrament so far, Cerim. I hope it stays that way.
Cerim! You have my thanks.
Not many square off against Darak and return holding their head high. Or with a head at all.
I pray Darak crawled under a rock somewhere to lick his wounds but... you don’t defend a city on prayers.
Perhaps it’s worth considering Odessa’s warning...
I’ve known her since she was a babe. But I’m not sure I know who’s in that cell.
I’m not blind to what drives the Risen. I’ve seen how people fall through the cracks.
But they’ve chosen their side, and I mine. Sometimes that’s all you can do.
Cerim - a moment?
If I might bend your ear, I’ve a proposition for you.
I saw how you dispatched the raiders in the old fortress. You’ve had a taste, any interest in the meal?
My men spotted the Risen warlord Darak in the Orban Glades.
He’s been a thorn in Ellsworth’s side for too long. I sent a contingent after him, but —
If you were to find yourself heading west, you might join them and do Sacrament a service.
We would all sleep better knowing Darak’s below ground.
Head west to hunt for Darak in the Glades. But keep your guard up for Risen. Or wolves. Or those damned Nith swamp tribes.
Just keep your guard up.
Ellsworth’s gone north, toward a dead-end I venture. While Odessa sits locked up in her cell.
Me, I’ve no patience for politics. And learned long ago not to get between the Governor and his daughter.
Warriors like us have a thirst that can be slaked in only one of two ways.
Ale and blood, my friend, ale and blood.
I come from a long line of potion masters. And I’m proud to say none of us have died by natural causes.
Well. Well...! That is surprising.
Ten thousand apologies. But I had to know if you were a true Cerim.
Iona's Bloom shows Cerim that which is otherwise left Unspoken... And poisons anyone else who touches it.
Perhaps you are worthy. Here – a token for your efforts, and for your most amusing foolishness.
You say you came by way of Sacrament? I hate the city – that stench and scurry.
But maybe there are more people there deserving of my gifts.
Yes, a decision! I shall enter its walls and offer my services. Once I catch this damned beetle.
Come come, little beetle. Don’t be shy. I’ve a mortar and pestle to introduce you to.
Why scurry in the dirt when you could flow through the blood? Purpose, it calls to you...
Watch where you’re walking! Another traveler blind to the bounty under their feet.
I am Markos, artist of alchemy, purveyor of potions.
If you’re looking for some swill that’ll turn your eyes yellow and your piss red, might I recommend a tavern?
Then again, you carry the markings of the Cerim. But are they the warnings of a pit viper’s stripes, or the illusion of eyes on a butterfly’s wings?
Then again, you carry the markings of the Cerim.
Care to prove yourself the genuine article and earn the right to taste my elixirs?
Inside this cave there is a rare and potent flower - Iona’s Bloom.
Find the bloom and, if you are Cerim, then I can make you the whore's promise - that you'll see God.
I hope you succeed. But if not... your blood would be a most interesting ingredient.
It’s all come to ruin.
All those poor souls in Marin... Homes. Families.
Now Odessa’s gone - she must’ve slipped out last night. And Ellsworth and Winnick have retreated to the War Room.
How could this have happened?
There must be an answer here in the Rookery. In one of these books or scrolls.
I just need to look harder. I’ll forgo food and sleep. But I don’t know which book... I don’t know where...
...I don’t know where to put my hands.
They claim the oak in the center of Marin shaded thirty generations under its branches.
Now it’s ash. All of it. The tree and those beneath it.
I always planned to die in one of two ways, Cerim.
A drunken old gizzard whose heart gives out in a brothel.
Or on the field of battle, surrounded by my enemies.
And to think I was starting to look forward to the former.
I hear Odessa was gone before daybreak. I wouldn’t hold it against you if you did the same.
Forsaken spare me…
I hear... nothing. The voices are gone. And so is he.
You cut out a piece of us so that we may live. But we are less for it.
En mirsa ella thallin. A Mender is to take no husband or wife. Only to serve the people.
It is a lonely life, and he was kind. There were times I wished for more.
Please, return to Marin. The Mother will guide me home.
I know the whispers in my mind were false. Of ancestors, of Menders come before.
But still, their comfort, their strength. That was real.
Now the only voice in my head is my own.
I’ve known death since I was a little girl. When she called, I was always gracious. But she never grows kinder.
Leave me, Cerim. The Mother will guide me home.
Keep your wits about you if you venture towards Marin.
Those woods were lawless before the plague ever took root.
Shhh…
If you make it to the temple, be careful. We’ve all gotten lost in the woods before. But never like this.
Go, Cerim. Look for the Winged Door. Silence these voices.
And beware the Balak Taw. Many travelers find them “charming”... until their eyes are pecked out and their skin clawed off.
I can't stay here.
I'll live with my sister in Sacrament. She screeches louder than the Balak Taw, but what choice do I have?
There's a stain left in my head, and I can't scrub it out. Not while I'm still here in Marin.
Nothing's changed. The crickets and owls sound the same. Hearth's just as warm. But everything's different.
I'll need a few days to pack my things. To say my goodbyes. Gods, what will I tell Irmgard?
Being Dasha means you don't feel safe anywhere, but Marin felt the closest yet. Or used to.
You did what you could, Cerim. It just wasn't enough.
After you cleared the temple, most of us came back to ourselves. But not my Hesta.
My wife's here but... she isn't. Like she lost something but can't say what.
Our son Will, he's in Sacrament. Please, if you see him, tell him his mother is fine.
If he knew the truth, he'd want to be here with her. And it's not safe.
Will's safer behind Sacrament's walls. It's what she would've wanted.
What she DOES want. She's... still here.
Come back to me, Hesta.
A Cerim in our village? The gods are cruel to bring you to us only now.
My wife can't seem to hear me anymore. Only the voices that beckon her into the forest.
Please... there must still be a way to wake her.
Won't be much of a village left at this rate...
Enjoy it, traveler. I don't think Marin Village will be here much longer. And it's got nothing to do with the plague.
Everyone just keeps moving to Sacrament. Like Hesta's boy. Gone to be a blacksmith's apprentice, I heard.
I understand the appeal of the big city. Used to live in Havenport myself. But we can't all be cobblers and musicians.
It's a vanishing way of life, ours. Rise with the sun. Listen to the forest. I'll miss this village when it's gone.
Do you hear it? The forest is speaking.
No, not the forest. There's someone... Calling to us...
Thank you, Cerim.
First traveler I've seen in ages...
I'm amazed you made it to our village at all, stranger. Hardly anyone comes here anymore.
The road 'tween here and Sacrament used to be a fine journey. Farmers, traders, peddlers. A right carriageway!
Back when Ellsworth first took over, it was almost like we were a part of Sacrament. That was a long time ago.
Don't remember whether the Balak Taw came first, or the Pestilence. But we might as well be an island now.
Through the meadows and into the forest. Then down the throat where the voice is born.
That is where we must go.
Won't be long before I can sell my wares again.
Thank you, Cerim.
Protect yourself against the Pestilence!
The finest shop in Marin! ...And the only one.
Don't brave the Marin Woods without seeing me first.
I'll look kindly on any referrals. Tell your friends, your family. Tell your enemies for all I care.
I'm not looking for the clamor of the city, but I could do with a few more voices in our village.
The Mountain Gate - now that's some damn fine masonry if I do say so myself. A job meant to last.
I'll gladly spit on the graves of those who knocked her down. But I hear they ain't got the luxury of a grave.
Heh. I'd know that shoddy craftsmanship anywhere.
So my clod of a cousin's still hammering away in Sacrament?
Figured they would've run him off by now. Chased him out of town with their crooked pitchforks and bent spears.
Eh, might as well give it here.
As any dishonest butcher will tell you - spoiled's a relative term.
Fillmore was always the runt of the litter. Swing too soft and bellows too cool, if you catch my drift.
Don't have a wife, don't want a wife. Ain't married to my anvil neither... but I'll still take her out on the town.
You gotta talk to the steel. Sweeten it up, baby it a bit. A quiet smithy means a brittle blade.
Let the spark of my swing light another under your arse.
Best steel on Sacra.
Ain't a girl half as pretty as the swing of a smithy...
A lovely sound to it, don't you think...
I know that song. That voice.
No one understands our love.
Her hair, oh her hair. Acres of it, lustrous and tawny, thick and pleasingly coarse.
You can keep your slender twigs - she has a body to her. Firm and sensual and low to the ground.
I love her wildness of spirit. I may live in the woods, but she truly makes the forest her home.
If a poem could only capture the music of her laugh, the long curve of her teeth, the depth of her eyes.
We don't have to be alone. Not anymore.
We're with them now.
Thank you, Cerim.
Look at the state of my house...
Don't know how long I was away. Feels like only a moment, but... I can see by the moss on my roof it wasn't.
Just when I was starting to get ahead of the weeds. Look at this garden now. Damned Goosefoot, it's everywhere.
I wouldn't live anywhere else, Cerim, but beating back this forest is a full-time job. Do you own a home?
Ugh... I suppose I'll have to re-patch the chimney now. The mold in this glen has a mind of is own.
Through the forest. Away from the village. That's where he is.
Far away from here...
What... what day is it? What... season is it?
Thank you, Cerim.
Sacra belongs to the Dasha, not just Marin Village.
We Dasha are a quiet, generous people, but some mistake humility for weakness.
Sacra has always been our home, even for the centuries we spent scattered across the Weeping Sea.
Someday Phalen will fall and where will we Dasha be? Right here.
Mother grow us, Maker build us, Seeker shepherd us, and Forsaken spare us.
The song. There's a sweetness to it. Like a lullaby.
Listen. Can you hear it?
Do you know how the Dasha came to Sacra?
The Mother raised this island from the sea. And she made the Dasha the sand along her shores.
The Maker built us out of bones and earth, right here on this very spot. We've always been here.
The Seeker called the Dasha here from across the wastes, and we flew together like starlings.
The Forsaken... Well. The Forsaken is why we've never left.
Finally... I know where we must go.
The path is open. We must walk together.
Thank you, Cerim.
It's so quiet now.
Where did they go? My mother's mother? My children's children?
The temple is empty now. All I hear is the gods' silence.
This can't be all of us. We used to be so many.
I can't hear Will. I can't hear any of them.
I can hear them. Calling to me.
I can hear Will. He sounds so happy. So peaceful.
I can't believe he's gone.
If the plague can defile someone as kindly as Caretaker Alden, what hope do any of us have?
The Pestilence isn't just an illness, it's a cruelty. It made monstrous what was best in Alden.
During thunderstorms he'd even let wolves shelter in the temple. Said it's what the Mother would want.
He liked to say: we're all just animals, and that's a blessing.
Please, you have to help them!
I don't know what's wrong with them. I can't wake them up!
The voices, the whispers, don't listen to them!
I'll write a book about it!
Yes yes, it's a tragedy what happened. But who said tragedies can't also be opportunities?
Someone has to tell this story. And that person should be compensated for such vital work, don't you agree?
We must make sure this never happens again by telling as many people as possible. As many copies as possible.
I was there in the thick of it. And I've always fancied myself a wordsmith. Who better to shoulder this burden?
"The Mad Caretaker!" No, maybe "A Plague Survivor's Tale!" Or "Rare Insights of a Mind Nearly Lost!"
What happened...
Feels like I'm waking from a long dream.
Not voices... a choir.
The song is softer, but I can still hear it. Woven into the trees.
Patient, I will be patient. I know he will return for us.
Something was lost, but I will find it. I was lost, but I'll be found.
Rot is growth. Silence is peace. I am us.
You know, not all Dasha are pacifists.
Darak the Risen warlord was born in my home village. Long before he felled men, he felled logs in the Marin Woods.
But the woman he desired gave her heart to another. A mainlander no less, with royal blood.
Darak attacked the outsider. Spilled blood within the sanctity of Marin's Sovann Circle.
The fight only stopped when Annora shamed Darak by invoking the name of the Forsaken against him.
She died many years later. I'm not sure how, but Darak never let it go.
Darak always hated the mainland. But after Annora's death, that hate curdled to fury and fire.
I can hear them all.
They're calling my name.
My thanks, Cerim.
Doesn't matter what you did, we don't want you here.
Look. We appreciate what you did for our village, but that don't mean you're not an outsider.
This hamlet gets by on keeping to ourselves, and protecting our own. You can't do either. So kindly move along.
Yes, the Dasha are friendly and quaint and all that. But we're not a carnival show. And we don't need your pity.
If it weren't for Irmgard I'd run you out of town myself. Nothing good will come from having you in our midst.
Murmurs in the leaves... you're going the wrong way...
We need to go to him...
Thank you, Cerim.
Beware the Balak Taw, Cerim.
You hear cawing from the treetops, the rustle of false feathers and then... the spears rain down.
Do they think themselves birds? Or simply worship them? I'd ask if they didn't answer only in screeches.
We all dream of flying, but wake up with our feet on the ground.
They roost in Marin Woods but have been known to migrate. Just like, well, you know.
We should pray. Among the voices.
At the temple. Where our prayers are heard. Where we hear our prayers. At the temple.
Dashan hala thas, Cerim. Peace begets peace.
When I heard the voices of those I know I'll soon see... I'm ashamed to say there was comfort in it.
Our infancy belongs to the Mother. Our youth to the Seeker. Our autumn to the Maker. And now...
I may be gone soon, but I'll go knowing I've left Marin a bit greener, a bit stronger than I met her.
Slow down, traveler. Life is the thing that your feet trample over as you race to find it.
He speaks for us.
He looks after us. He'll keep us safe.
I... I can't explain it.
It felt like all my fear was gone. My worries and cares and concerns. My thoughts.
Imagine if moss had grown over me, rooted me to the spot right there in the Woods…
Thank you, Cerim. ...I think? Freedom feels like... the weight of the sky on my back.
I know the Caretaker is gone, but it's like a tiny seed of him lives still in my mind. Waiting again to bloom.
Shhh you must be quiet.
The quieter you are, the better you can hear them. Hear him.
Thank you, Cerim, for helping us.
I pity those poor souls lost in Caylen, but I confess I hold no pity for the loss of the city itself.
Cities are like cankers on the skin of the world. They're brittle, and they make us brittle too. Brittle and deaf.
Ten thousand blessings, Cerim, for returning us to ourselves.
The forest is meant for many voices, not just one drowning out all others.
The birdsong. The rustle of leaves. The chitter and hoot and howl.
You returned us to our nature. Allow me to offer nature's bounty back.
No ailment exists that nature hasn't already provided a remedy for. Our insights pale before her own.
The forest offers herself up as our home, why should we not allow our bodies to be the forest's home?
I'll never understand those who fear the grave. What could be more comforting than warm soil and roots' embrace?
Not a moth crushed. Not a stem broken.
Nourish your body and ease your mind.
The forest provides.
At last we are one with the world...
In the meadow, I am the meadow. Let the grass grow over my voice.
I should go to them.
There are so many voices. Calling me home.
Many of the villagers are still finding themselves, remembering which voices were their own.
But still, it is a blessing to be able to hear oneself think again.
My sister and I only found Marin Village recently, and already thought we'd lost it.
We were raised in Caylen, cleaning stables. Left only days before the Mountain Gate shut.
Can't say I miss all those haughty clerics and church bells.
Things are better here. Quieter. We can practice our faith in peace.
You're always welcome here, Cerim. Everyone is.
Except maybe those Caylen holymen. How can just one god demand so much?
I nearly lost myself.
My brother was locked up for two years in Fort Reach. Said he half lost his mind. Now I think I know how he felt.
That Madrigal's a fool, tearing down the Mountain Gate. We need more walls now, not less. Walls in our heads too.
Plague made one old man into a monster that nearly broke our village. Imagine what it'll do with all of Caylen.
The mainland god and all its hands… Didn't feel so different from the Caretaker in my head.
IRMGARD: En thassa lewwin theen halel.
IRMGARD: It's Alden, the Caretaker. He doesn't want to be alone.
IRMGARD: His voice reaches out from the Temple of Day and Night, barricaded behind the eyes of the dead.
IRMGARD: Maybe if I had gone to him, it would have saved them. There could have been another way.
IRMGARD: I was their Mender...
ODESSA: You are their Mender. And there may well be another way.
IRMGARD: The Gods may lack mercy, but not a sense of humor.
IRMGARD: Yes, I know what you are, Cerim. A prayer come too late.
ODESSA: You found her.
ODESSA: Irmgard, I -
IRMGARD: Oh no. Not you too, my dear… You shouldn’t be here.
IRMGARD: I’ve been gathering herbs to... I don’t know. Do what the last bundle could not. And the one before that.
IRMGARD: Your father asked me to sing the Fir'twah at the Rites of the Fallen...
IRMGARD: But how can I sing for them when I can't even protect them?
ODESSA: Irmgard - What happened here?
The Temple can be reached from above. But the Balak Taw own the treetops.
Here - I took this off that Mad Brambler in the village. It will get you into their territory.
Look for the Winged Door. You’ll... know it when you see it.
There will be more than Balak Taw to contend with. Alden cared for all creatures great and small. Now they serve his twisted memory.
The Cerim will find a way. Let’s get you back to Marin. No medicine can stop this sickness now.
ODESSA: Cerim. Of course. You’re like a pebble in this island’s shoe, aren’t you?
ODESSA: I must find Mender Irmgard. The note on her door says she’s gone west in search of a remedy.
ODESSA: Your choices are your own, Cerim. But Marin is worth saving.
ODESSA: I normally give a better show. But these Balak Taw are getting bolder.
ODESSA: Why are you here? To help - or to prey on the weak like these vultures?
ODESSA: No bars between us now.
ODESSA: My mother’s… My horn.
ODESSA: I... thought I’d lost it.
ODESSA: You are anything but predictable, Cerim.
ODESSA: There’s something... wrong with the village. Can you hear it?
ODESSA: A voice beneath the wind... Calling me...
Used to be, the Balak Taw wouldn’t dare set foot in Marin. Their territory is the trees.
But this sickness has... turned our island against itself.
I can hear my father’s voice in my head, telling me to enter the woods. Is that what he said?
And another voice, a woman. She sounds like...
Like a stranger I’ve known all my life.
We must look for Irmgard through the caves to the west. This village needs its Mender.
I used to have to drag Annora to this circle. She never wanted to pray. But she was happy to clamber all over the stones.
I... I close my eyes, and still I cannot quite picture her.
Your father doesn’t speak of her?
Never. She has a name and a grave. Nothing more.
He carries his burden as best he can, as we all do. Perhaps we in Marin can lighten yours, Cerim.
ODESSA: So it’s done. This village owes you a debt of gratitude, Cerim.
ODESSA: And your voice is still strong, Irmgard. You'll sing again - in this Circle. And in Sacrament at the Rites. For them.
IRMGARD: Will I see you there? All of us at one table again.
ODESSA: ...I'm not welcome in Sacrament.
IRMGARD: The Rites are a time of peace. Not only to honor the dead, but for the living to make amends.
ODESSA: Irmgard, I... I've unfinished business to the east.
IRMGARD: I see. Then may the Seeker guide you safely...
IRMGARD: ...and the Mother bring you home.
ODESSA: ... As do I.
ODESSA: They’ve brought him back?
IRMGARD: Alden was... one of us. Even the Pestilence cannot change that.
IRMGARD: So many gone. The Caretaker. Your mother. Even you... I know you won't stay.
Ellsworth asked me to sing the Fir'twah at the Rites of the Fallen. But I can’t...
How can I serve as Mender when I cannot mend myself?
ODESSA: I remember when my mother used to sing me to sleep. You did too. The same lullaby.
ODESSA: She’s not gone. None of them are.
Marin's not my concern. But you might find the forest suits your interests, Cerim.
The boy speaks the truth - my scouts have reported the Pestilence running rampant there.
They say you... hear it, before you see it.
Not sure what to make of that.
Please, go to Marin Village. Through the northern gate, past the cemetery.
And someday when I’m the smith, all your work will be free of charge!
Will you help, Cerim?
Randolph and his men don’t care about anyone outside Sacrament’s walls.
But lots of us got family in Marin. Even Odessa was born there.
I only moved here to apprentice for Fillmore.
I used to visit more, but my parents asked me to stay put in Sacrament.
They said the forest is too dangerous.
But they’ve never gone this long without sending word!
Marin is not my responsibility. Now get on with you.
Cerim, please, will you make him listen?
To what? We’ve long known the plague is loose in the Marin Woods.
But this is different! No one’s heard from the village for days. My parents –
- live outside our walls. My duty is to Sacrament. Those beyond her gates must fend for themselves.
If the Cerim wish to indulge your hysterics, that’s their concern. But if you ask me, the Dasha are precisely where they belong.
And where’s that?
Not here.
Hmm, not a birdman, and not Dasha neither.
So are you lost or dense? Maybe a touch of both?
Marin ain’t safe for travelers anymore. Ain’t safe for anyone. Best place for you is back in Sacrament.
But don’t wanna listen to me? So be it.
Your skull will make a fine Balak Taw headdress, if the Blight don’t get you first.
Who am I? I’m nobody to nobody. Just a pair of eyes watching the comings and goings. More goings of late.
Feathered savages, the lot of ‘em.
Only the foolish or the desperate would try to reason with the Balak Taw.
Didn’t realize that old Dasha Caretaker was both.
Never would’ve believed it if I hadn’t seen it with my own eyes. Him pleading with them, voice all aquiver.
He told ‘em that the Blight creeping forth from his temple threatens the whole wood.
That we’re all caretakers - the Dasha on the ground and Balak Taw in the treetops. Brothers of the forest.
And what did they do? Pecked out his damn eyes. Clawed his face to tatters. Dumped his broken body on the temple steps.
He said he was out of ideas to stop the plague's spread. Guess they had one more of their own.
I like the Dasha, I really do. But it ain’t coincidence that they wind up written off every page of history.
It’s because they never learn - the world ain’t built for the kind, the generous.
The Pestilence takes what it wants. So do the Balak Taw. So does the mainland.
You want peace? That’s what a grave’s for.
Me? I just scratch out a low to the ground living. No land, no coin, no attention given. Pigs get fed, hogs get slaughtered.
Sacrament's gates are always open to those in need, or those who keep her safe. Help yourself to our food and shelter.
But leave the ale to me, ha!
The Watcher waits for you in the rookery.
You must gather, Cerim. The Watcher awaits.
Hey! Cerim... over here, come on then.
I knew it... Should’ve never brought you on board.
You’ll never make it to Sacrament from here.
This coast is crawling with the Risen.
Oh. The waves. Can you feel them, Father?
We’re back at sea…
Be careful, Lara! Someone’s coming!
A Cerim! Forgive my father, he mistook you for one of the Risen.
If you make for Sacrament, there are worse things than bandits up ahead. A great beast is loose in these Glades.
They say it used to be a man. I wanted to go after it, but father says —
Father says the Torn are not to be trifled with. And he’s right.
I don’t fear the Pestilence any more than a wild boar. One day they’ll sing songs about my skill with a bow!
I’d prefer you alive to sing them yourself, daughter.
If you can make it to Sacrament, God embrace you. But my daughter and I know better – we’re heading for the Lowland Meadows.
That’s where the rest of our hunting party is. They’ll never believe we met a Cerim!
You’re welcome to our fire as long as you’re here. I’ll keep it tended for you.
We both know what it’s like to be lost in the woods, and all you can think about it is a warm meal!
If you’re short of things to cook in the fire, keep your eyes peeled around the Glades.
A true hunter should never be above foraging in the underbrush!
Thank you, stranger. Thought I could sabotage the gate, keep more of these savages from reaching Sacrament’s walls.
But I got my damn fool self trapped too.
Suppose there’s a reason I’m a blacksmith and not a soldier. Name’s Fillmore.
If you ever need anything repaired, you come to me. Nothing I can’t fix.
Now here! This will open the gate. Get yourself to Sacrament - through the Orban Glades to the east. It’s the safest place for both of us.
But keep a careful eye out. I heard some of these Risen speak of a... foul presence outside the city’s gate.
You go on ahead, clear the road. I can’t fix nothing if I’m dead in a ditch.
Figured I’d be safer camping out here. You let me know if you need anything repaired.
Sickening stench isnt it? All those bodies, ripped apart... God save the soul who comes face to face with the cause of all this.
Can’t thank you enough for helping me out earlier. The road was clear all the way from the fortress. Impressive work.
How’s that, you bastards!! Who’s squealing now?! Ha!
Please, I dont have it!
Look, just give us back the gate switch, smithy, and we’ll let you pass.
Bet I can make ‘em squeal so loud even Ellsworth hears it.
Leave me be! I’m no soldier and I have no coin!
Haha. What’s that smell? He pissin’ himself?
Do you see the outfit? The weapon? Where and how I'm standing? That's because I'm on duty.
Unless Ellsworth sent you, I don't care.
If you're so intrigued by our cages, why don't you hop inside one?
A few nights in a cage will cure your curiosity, I promise.

Cerim... 
Couldn’t be anyone else.
I’m not one to spend a lot of time kneeling in churches. But what happened at the Gate... a man’s got questions.
Not saying I’m out here making amends. Not saying I’m not either. But it helps to have powerful friends.
And who’s more powerful than You Know Who.
Look for the lighthouse if you want to reach that wreck.
And don’t take this the wrong way, but with any luck we’ll never lay eyes on each other again.
Nothing… It’s nothing…
Cerim. Hm. I suppose you have no fear of the Pestilence at all. Do you believe the Madrigal?
She brought an army. And a will to match it. Perhaps I’ve grown too accustomed to retreat.
It’s said that your people built this gate during the first war with the plague.
When it fell a year ago, you could hear it in every corner of the island, like thunder.
It woke me from a deep sleep. One I feel I’ve never quite returned to.
Even if you heed the Madrigal’s request, be careful.
There’s a fell wind coming from that cavern to the west.
Tender of the Words. Speaker of the Dead. Those Who Walk Between the Rain.
There’s a beauty to the old names, even in their heresy.
Surprised I recognize you, Cerim? I used to sneak into the archives at night to read stories of your people.
The church considered it forbidden knowledge. Old fools hiding from what they don’t understand.
But I think we understand each other.
There is an inscription at the base of the gate. It speaks of a chamber to the west - a means of opening the way.
This is why you’re here.
Go to the chamber, and be seen by your god. Let your presence be my passage.
Many in the Church see you as a blight to be stamped out.
Prove them wrong, Cerim. Go to the chamber, open the gate.
Have you ever seen Caylen, Cerim?
Twice a day her cathedral bells call out for grace, and twice a day her many voices answer.
I will let you see her, if you help me.
See her restored to glory.

The gate to the holy city did not fall shut without reason. 
The ancients built it to defend against the plague!
The ancients are dead, Governor.
It’s our duty, not theirs, to save the people of Caylen.
Can you not hear them yourself, crying out for help? Calling us through the stone?
I hear nothing.
The mountain won’t yield to your words the way men do.
Of course it will. All I need is someone who speaks its language.
Strange expedition this one.
Don't mind saying this backwater wasn't my first choice, but a knight of House Bolein always answers their King's call.
For nearly a century House Bolein has sat at the head of the Empire's table. Know why?
Not the church and its eerie little minions. Rather the blood and sweat of its finest knights.
With any luck we'll be back on the mainland soon without expending too much of either.
Don't linger too long, stranger, my men are fond of target practice.
Was something supposed to happen?
Ancient plagues, mystical forces, buried secrets. Nonsense.
You know how you know what's real? You can stick it with a pike.
Something tells me this is gonna mean more work for me and mine.
Better lifting stones than fending off Kylesh marauders or putting down Waithe fanatics.
But I wouldn't say no to a bit of action, warm my blood a bit.
I can't say much for the grandeur of God, but it's quite a monument to the might of men.
Lotta work to crack an egg.
Heresy...
Can you feel your dead here, Cerim?
I feel them.
Their fingertips clawing against the bottom of my feet.
Your foolish kind, thinking they were building walls, gates, temples.
They built only tombs.
You are but the twitch of a dead thing's leg.
Your dead god laughs at you.
Do not fear, charlatan, our true God will do what you never could.
Perhaps you may find the same purpose your people found - to feed the soil.
You may linger, Cerim, and witness what a living faith can achieve.
There is no labor when it is in God's name.
Our great engine knocks at salvation's door.
The time has come.
God's hands will enfold you.
There is a place for you here...
The void inside you can be filled.
Throw down your weapons, and wait for his Embrace.
Soon you will feel His fingers wrapping around your mind... His hand around your skull.
This is Salvation.
You will understand before the end.
Take it as a sign...
There is no Sayer. There is no other light.
The only path lies with us.
We will wait for you.
What you see being built here is not a work of Man.
It is not the sweat of these slaves that will bring down the gate - it is the gentle touch of the Eternal.
Can you feel him in the air?
Now that I see it built... Now that I hear the shuddering of the stone, I... I must confess...
...I am not sure what awaits us on the other side.
What have we done?
The many hands.
Begone. You have no business in the Nameless Pass.
Go back to your kind, Cerim, and ask them why? Why were you born? Why not end this lineage of torment?
May your next of kin find stillborn peace.
The eye within.
Who speaks to us?
One who slips between God’s fingers.
None may pass. By order of the Madrigal.
The Cerim do not hear. They have no ears, nor eyes, nor tongue for speaking.
They understand only death.
Flee, Unspoken. Lest we begin to speak your language.
The many hands...
We cleansed the pass of God's unwanted...
...washed it down to purest stone.
And yet look now what crawls forth...
...one, it seems, that God forgot.
Go, silent one. See the Madrigal if you must.
Perhaps she will be the last thing you see...
This order is an act of grace.
It is her desire, not ours.
As you have separated yourself from God, soon may you find your soul separated from your body.

Your head from your neck.
Your eyes from your skull.
Perhaps one day we will cleanse this island of even you.
She will speak with the Cerim...
The Madrigal... requests your presence. You must make your way through the Nameless Pass, and seek her audience.
At the heretics’ gate.
At the pagan door.
This is the will of god.
Many lives ago, your kind fought the curse. The Madrigal believes you may be of service again.
As God finds meaning even in broken things... So does she.
Go east. Toward the sound of steel and flesh.
The sound of deliverance.
Find the Madrigal at the gate. Go, or be taken.

The many hands.
The eye within.
We should not linger, Cerim.
The Madrigal has no further use for us. Or for reason it seems. But you can still be of use in Sacrament.
I pray we both make it back in one piece.
Although... what waits for me in Sacrament cannot be tamed with swords and spears.
What must it be like, to have no true name? To be defined by that which you seek to kill?
I imagine it like a pit within your chest.
And all you can do is dig deeper.
How disappointing. Even your own history rejects you.
I should have known better. Believing I could find purpose in the last descendant of a failed race.
But my purpose is clear. I have given my life to God a thousand times over. And God, in turn, has made my life an arrow.
An arrow pointed straight through this stone, at the heart of the rot in Caylen.
Go now, Cerim. This is not your story. Not anymore.
This gate will fall, Cerim. And the old ways will fall with it.
Sure you wanna head that way?
Nothing that direction but a wrecked quarry, a closed gate, and now an army of Inquisitors. Disquieting they are.
I see Ellsworth marching with 'em. Finally graces the Pass with his presence.
"How you living, Orvyn? Could you use help with the farm, Orvyn?" Nah, he didn't say nothing.
Mainland looks down at her isles. Sacrament at those living outside her gates. No difference.
Admiring my farmstead, my little slice of heaven?
Used to be at least.
Guards march prisoners to the quarry - I sell 'em turnips. Guards march home - I sell more turnips.
Then the plague. Quarry riots. Brigands and Boarskin on the road. Had a wife - now I got a plot.
Is Orvyn leaving? Eh, maybe tomorrow. Always tomorrow.
You should've seen this place when the Mountain Gate was open and the quarry thriving.
A right highway. Plum real estate. Now it's just a warning, a road sign - "death ahead."
Quarry’s done for. So am I. You’ve come too late.
You... You’re not the Inquisition. You’re something else.
They came like a fire. Not seeing, only burning. Marching toward the Mountain Gate. Left us to die...
But some prisoners fled before the Madrigal came. Sought safety in the Cerim ruins to the north.
The two who led the escape - they were the worst of us all. The Riven Twins.
If the Torn don’t kill you, they surely will.
The ones who put me in here... I only wish I could have my hands around their throat before I turn.
That would be a fine ending.
Guards abandoned us when the Pestilence came. Left the healthy chained to the sick.
And the Inquisitors burned anyone unlucky enough to still be alive.
If you make it to the ruins of your kind, ask your god what we did to deserve this.
Mine’s not answering.
Too long... I’ve lived too long... To see such foulness return.
What is it?
A Watcher regards but never interferes. A Watcher observes but never affects.
Wait, is this... it’s an effigy.

“Sinew, husk, and marrow tamed.
Healed by fire, sickened by flame.”
Cerim, perhaps if you burn the effigy in a plagued fire...
...we can banish it once more.
But what happens if it’s burned in a pure fire?
Blood. Ash. Death.
The nights I’ve spent in this rookery, scouring books and old scrolls for a secret, a cure, a weapon.
When perhaps you were the weapon all along, Cerim.
It sounds as if the creature you fought was almost a shade or imprint of one you’ve faced before. A recollection.
Could the plague have a memory? But that which has a memory has a mind.
Curious. Most curious.
Bad to worse.
Did you put in a good word for us, Cerim? Poke your nose where it don't belong?
No? Doesn't matter. Now look at us!
Winnick promoted us right back on the wall! Like serving up a meal to those flying beasts.
He said he "had faith in us." Didn't like the sound of that, not one bit.
I can't be risking my life up here. I've got a family to take care of!
Who? Elga?
Well... She could be family. I'm planning ahead, eyeing the future.
Do me a favor and keep both those eyes on the skies. Elga's not gonna wed a corpse.
If you manage to spread word that we're not deserving of our duties, it'd be much appreciated, Cerim.
Could they... The Unspoken, who came too late... Could they...?
Foolish to hope. Foolish not to. A coin with a fool on both sides.
Was I... Unspoken? Long ago?
Or have I simply... forgotten to speak?
The mind is... a burrow. A dark hole... filled with muck and vermin.
But sometimes, perhaps... It can be a haven. For long winters.
Like a keening. A blackened prayer. The voices of the lost.
If a prayer can be answered, then it can be silenced.
The Pestilence. It has a sound to it. When the night is still, you can hear it. Whispering.
Down in the darkness, my... mind was...
Waiting. Listening...
There was... an imp. Gnawing at me. Scratching at my wits.
I leaned in... closer, until I could see his true form...
It was the question.
...Why has it returned?
More ichor. This one... flecked with sadness. The girl’s eyes were open as it took her.
Do you know where your kind came from, Cerim...?
From death. First there was the plague. Then came the Cerim.
Your paths are woven together. When one ends, perhaps, so shall the other.
Here... Give it here.
You’ve brought them! A... menagerie of the grotesque.
What are you making, Master?
Amends.
SELINE: All I ever had was purpose.
SELINE: I won't stand by as the people of Caylen perish.
SELINE: They will ask how God saved his faithful.
SELINE: And we will say -
SELINE: He brought down mountains.
SELINE: With many eyes you see my future. With many hands you protect my journey.
SELINE: With many eyes you see my future. With many hands... you protect my journey.
SELINE: With many eyes… you…
Are you proud of your time here, Cerim?
Did you come to Sacra to serve frightened old men?
I’ve known such men my whole life. Those who nurture their fear like a child.
Who talk for hours, who fill whole tomes explaining why the right thing to do is always... nothing.
I came from nothing. I was no one.
WATCHER: Do you hear it?
WATCHER: Go, Cerim! Quickly. If she knocks hard enough, the city will answer.
WATCHER: And Caylen is no longer a city of men.
ROAN: Master, you’re awake! I -
WATCHER: Be quiet, boy! For once in your life, listen, do not speak.
WATCHER: Do you hear it?
ROAN: Thunder?
WATCHER: In a way.
