WATCHER: A lost daughter returns home, faith and flame at her back.
WATCHER: Your kind spoke the words that sealed the gate. But no closed door ever stopped her before.
ROAN: Do you mean the vanguard? The Madrigal?
Cerim, please gather. I must speak to you.
Cerim, thank the Embrace you’ve come.
ROAN: It’s the Watcher. I don’t know what’s happened.
ROAN: He’s made such strides of late, his faculties returning,
ROAN: but today I found him, well, lapsed.
ROAN: At first I thought it was a figment of my...
ROAN: nervous demeanor, but no - he won’t eat, nor drink.
ROAN: He won’t speak. His breath is far too shallow.
ROAN: I’m unable to rouse him, and I fear his condition has somehow worsened...
Do as he says, Cerim. Return to the Mountain Gate and stop the Madrigal.
Fly, Cerim. Back through the Nameless Pass. If the Gate falls, so may Sacra.
Hope is new, but time is short. And the world pivots on small axes.
It is... the strength of your kind.
Come, Cerim. Let the dark into your veins.
You must bend death to your will.
You looked upon the holy city - or what was left of it -  didn’t you? I can see it in your eyes.
Caylen may be lost, but we aren’t. Not yet.
The Pestilence, it threatens to swallow us all. Randolph’s men report outbreaks all over Sacra.
Alistair, please. If ever your wisdom was needed, it’s now.
He was lucid before, I swear. But his mind is like... the sun dipping in and out of the clouds.
He rifles through old journals and tomes, scrawling the same thing over and over in the margins.

“Sinew, husk, and marrow tamed.
Healed by fire, sickened by flame.”
What does it mean?
Perhaps nothing. Or perhaps the plague carries its own death within it. If there’s an answer, I fear we won’t find it here.
Look, it's the Cerim
We heard the ram fall silent, and then...
Did you see those demons in the sky?
They expect us to stand against those things?
What are we to do?
Why would he care what that old man has to say?
What happened at the Gate?
Was this your doing, Cerim?
I don't belong on the wall.
Ellsworth'll see us through.
If only he would speak to me. I  wish to be of service, to play my part in our preservation, but... his silence is deafening.
There must be an answer here in the Rookery. In one of these books or scrolls.
I just need to look harder. I’ll forgo food and sleep. But I don’t know which book... I don’t know where...
...I don’t know where to put my hands.
Far be it for me to command your efforts, Cerim, but we’ve no one else.
You must do what we cannot. Face the Pestilence where it has taken deepest root. Our salvation may lie within.
Yes. For too long the plague has twisted our own bodies against us. Let us return the favor.
And if you uncover any of the... foul anatomy the Watcher wrote of, please, bring it here. Perhaps it will awaken something within him.
Oh good, you’re awake. Please, Cerim, you must see this.
Forgive the... grotesque display. We - pruned some of the poor Torn soul you killed at our gates.
I left a vial of its blood here on the table. But when I returned, I found it... altered.
The Watcher, he - he must’ve refined it. Purified it. An ancient technique.
Now you just need to - to - to - to -
I apologize. I - it’s my nerves.
The ichor must flow through your veins. The scrolls say it gives strength to your kind.
Go to the Watcher. This skill is beyond me.
Go to the Watcher.
There. Now, if you should encounter any more of the Torn - collect their ichor and bring it to the Watcher.
And if you ever want to know the comings and goings within our fair city’s walls, I’m your man.
Roan - scholar, guide, inquisitive soul, unrepentant gossip - at your service!
I dream of them. Their limbs twist but do not break. Their flesh smears like oil. And the hunger in their eyes...
I... Where is Roan?
Are you...? Roan, come here! There’s a stranger in the rookery.
Why have you come?
The chamber has spoken again!
More gauntlets, twisting up the stairs. Yet they draw us ever deeper...
Another statue has come to life. Perhaps this pit is truly endless.
Another ancient one seeks your offering, Cerim.
Voices of the dead... Cerim, look!
Another trial has awoken.
How much will this chamber keep growing?
More gauntlets. More savagery. More chances to be torn apart or hacked to bits.
Gods, I envy you.
I wonder how many times you will spill blood for the Sayer.
Perhaps her thirst can never be quenched.
It’s like this place is... burrowing inside my mind.
This chamber keeps shifting, Cerim. I turn my back and new marvels appear from the shadows.
Is it your doing? Perhaps you are molding the world to your liking... just as the ancients did.
I must accept that I will never know such powers. No matter how much I read.
...The Sayer will never speak to me.
What is my purpose here, Cerim?
This is how you were forged. How your kind learned to sculpt the world...
But where is my crucible?
I wish I could have met him.
...I had no idea what awaited you below, Cerim. I hope you suffered many great deaths.
Oh, to know what it would have been like, felled by his sword, even once!
The Echo Knights are... a part of this place. I do not think we have seen the last of them.
But I fear these trials may have come... unmoored.
If you return here, I am not sure what you will find. Be ready for anything.
The gardeners are dead. And so the garden grows wild.
I recognize this... It’s the same inscription as out here. Only...
This tablet is complete.
“We remember the chosen five, our fiercest Unspoken, who fought these trials through wrath and silence..."
“...Yet the endless gauntlet took them to madness. Now Cerim are no longer forged here, they are hunted.”
“Abandon this place, for they still stalk these chambers..."
“There is no trial of the worthy. Only death. Forever the Tomb of the Echo Knights.”
I’m not finished here, Cerim. And I doubt you are either.
This place has more secrets to divulge. The dead stacked below our feet like a foundation of bone.
Who built these trials? What keeps them churning? How deep does it go?
We’ll find the answers. The past speaks in whispers, but you and I know how to hear them.
What did it feel like? For your story to be untold, and then told again?
Look, Cerim, I’ve found a new inscription...
“We remember the chosen few - Cyvion, and his fiercest Unspoken, who fought these trials through wrath and silence..."
...I can’t read the next part, this stone is all but crumbled. Then it just says:
“...forever the Tomb of the Echo Knights.”
Damn. I wish I could decipher more. Cerim - can you think of anyone who might be versed in ancient texts like this?
There’s a story here... begging to be told.
It sounds like a group of mighty warriors are buried here. Quite an honor.
I’m sure you’re no layabout yourself.
Follow in their footsteps, Cerim. And perhaps someday history will sing your praises, alongside the Echo Knights.
Please - tell me as soon as you learn anything more about the Echo Knights buried here!
Was it a good death this time? Do you carry them all with you, or is each like a small weight cast off?
Well what are you standing there for? Go on, bring back more Fallen Embers! We must keep going.
So you read it in the original tongue without using the Sir Agustin Codex?
Naturally. Don’t you?
...Of course.
It’s just providence to meet another soul passionate about history.
Perhaps you could tell me of... your own history?
You know, most assume I come from a family of mortuary owners, gravekeepers, tombstone carvers.
My mother bakes pies. My father builds roofs.
My first introduction to the hereafter was them boring me to death.
That’s very funny. It was meant to be funny, yes?
My family was never interested in meaning. But I was. I wanted to know the “why” behind things.
But I don’t know if there is a “why” to this place...
Cerim, have you met - well, yes, of course you have.
I just had to come down and s - - s - see this place for myself. Fantastic, isn’t it?
If there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s that the Cerim don’t have much to say.
Fortunately I’m spared that affliction! I’ve always been prone to blather on or stumble forward, while wiser souls bite their tongue or —-
Move back.
Yes, precisely! You understand.
No, move back. You’re standing in my light.
Oh, my apologies.
I must return to the rookery. My first duty is to my m - ma - m - mas - m - to the Watcher.
Very well. And please... Roan, was it?
Yes!
Try not to damage anything on the way out. Your footsteps seem a bit careless.
Cerim! There you are. Look at this.
The floor of the masonry collapsed, revealing this chamber below. Isn’t it remarkable?
No one’s breathed this air for a thousand years.
I believe a deeper ruin lies beyond this seal. But I’m unsure how to access it…
You know in some cultures, the faithful pleased their gods by ritualistically disemboweling themselves.
Wouldn’t that be a sight?
I’ve pored over every inch of this chamber, but it refuses to speak to me. Maybe it will listen to you?
Cerim - will you share your death with me?
Death is a lost art. People trip in the street, drown in creeks, choke on chicken bones.
But your kind perfected the form.
That’s why I’ve devoted my life to studying you. Your ruins. Your ways. Your slaughter.
Sorry, I never introduced myself. I am Elsa, a historian.
There are relics of your kind all over Sacra. Another was just discovered in the stone mason’s shop, by the cemetery.
You should see it for yourself! Perhaps it’s your temple, your library. Your tomb?
This city was built atop the graves of the ancients.
Come find me in the mason’s shop and I’ll show you just what I mean.
Have you been written from the whispers? Are you my death?
...You’re really here. A Cerim in Sacrament! So the Watcher was right - you came.
Tell me - can you feel it? That flickering in the air?
There are spots like this one all over Sacra, a prickling, as if something lies... just beyond my vision.
But it’s stronger here than anywhere else.
I’m convinced this is the site of some ancient, vital Cerim remnant. Perhaps a nexus of sorts?
I feel almost as if I could just... reach out and grasp it. And it me.
Another trial has awoken! Here, Cerim, show me what you found.
...I... I’m sorry, Cerim. I didn’t know.
Perhaps we should do as it says and abandon this place.
Or perhaps... a true death awaits us both.
...I had no idea what awaited you below, Cerim. I hope you suffered many great deaths.
This place has more secrets to divulge. The dead stacked below our feet like a foundation of bone.
Who built these trials? What keeps them churning? How deep does it go?
Yes, yes, that’s it! Your blood was the key!
Astonishing. This is the largest Cerim ruin I’ve ever seen.
And there’s that feeling in the air again... Can you sense it?
How strange. It’s the same as that spot near the square...
Yesssss... Your ancestors. They are here.
Can you feel their breath prickling your skin?
See what lies below, Cerim. Go to your glory. To your end.
Perhaps they are one and the same.
I think I know what this place was... a training ground!
The ancient Cerim built it to hone their skills as they fought against the plague.
Each of these statues will lead to a gauntlet. Stitched together from different times, places, dreams.
But the inscription says we need a Fallen Ember to begin the trials - have you seen them?
They lie strewn about the island. Only the Cerim can touch them, for they burn like stars.

Wait, you - you’ve found one.
 Hm.
The old ones believed that when the Sayer spoke the first words, they set the sky ablaze - and the embers rained down into our world.
I think they’re fragments of a broken star myself.
Quickly! Give the ember to the statue. Make an offering as you did before.
It’s as though there’s a wire inside my skull. Can you feel it too?
I feel there must be something in this room with us...
Bring me an Ember if you can.
Each of us is born for dying. All we get to choose is how.
Well, what are you waiting for? Go on! Make an offering - just a drop should do it. You’ve got plenty!
See what lies below, Cerim. Go to your glory. To your end.
Perhaps they are one and the same.
You know most assume I come from a family of mortuary owners, gravekeepers, tombstone carvers.
Truth is, my mother bakes pies. My sister mends shoes. My father builds roofs.
My first introduction to the hereafter was them boring me to death.
I studied under Ciprio the Elder. Have you heard of him?
Of course not. He specialized in the lineage and trade history of horse owners.
I’ll never understand why people obsess over the details of a life, but not what matters most - how it ends.
I hope to see you again soon. I feel... calm in your presence. Like I’m speaking to history itself.
With others I feel... unmoored. Their empty chatter. Their trivial squabbles.
I should have been born in the past.
By the gods...
The Sayer speaks to you! You’ve awoken the chamber.
What’s this? A book?
Who’s Roan? Oh, I didn’t realize the Watcher had an apprentice.
Well let’s have a look.
I recognize this... It’s the same inscription as out here. Only...
This one is complete.
“We remember the chosen few, Cyvion and his fiercest Unspoken, who fought these trials through wrath and silence..."
“...Yet the endless gauntlet took them to madness. Now Cerim are no longer forged here, they are hunted.”
“Abandon this place, for Cyvion and his shades still stalk these chambers..."
“There is no trial of the worthy. Only death. Forever the Tomb of the Echo Knights.”
No... No no, it can’t be.
There must be a purpose to this place. A meaning.
It can’t just be... chaos.
The world above, that endless rabble, that is chaos. But the ancients were wise, were mighty. They knew.
...Didn’t they?
What do we do, Cerim - press on? But towards what end? Were there ever any answers here?
The gardeners are dead. And so the garden grows wild.
Cerim! Cerim, I must speak with you.
A Watcher, as you know, must be a meticulous steward of ancient Cerim texts.
Of course... It is forbidden for an apprentice to... go snooping through his master’s...
Um - well - never mind where it came from. I found it! A copy of Elsa’s inscription. But... complete.
Please - take this book to Elsa for me.
Tell her it’s from Roan. I mean if she asks. She knows who I am, of course. Probably.
One must always cite one's sources!
The full inscription is... well, maybe I mistranslated. Elsa will know better.
Oh, hello again. I... hear you’ve met Elsa, our local historian.
Or, well - not local, I suppose. In point of fact she’s an outsider, just as I am. From Havenport, I believe.
Or so I’ve heard. Or may have heard. We’re just acquaintances - colleagues. Er, associates. Oh, dear...
Right. She told me about her find, beneath the cemetery. Wonderful, isn’t it?
But this inscription she unearthed... Echo Knights is it? Hmm, I swear I’ve come across that phrase before.
Perhaps I should do a bit of “digging” myself... in the literary sense.
The Watcher’s library is vast. Perhaps there is a tome here that could help Elsa. I mean, Elsa’s research, of course!
Thank you for keeping watch. But I fear we have wasted your time. Lord Baurus is an old friend. He posed no threat.
His words bore enough threat on their own.
I tell you - I didn’t like any of that.
Not sure it was wise for the Cerim to hear all that...
They do not seem the talkative type.
I tell you - I didn’t care for any of that. Mainland schemes washing up on our shores.
Do you think she suffered?
...Who?
Reed’s daughter. I wonder... What was the last thing he said to her? I hope a kindness.
Ellsworth. We may be on the cusp of war, of ruin. Her death was a tragedy, but right now we must focus on what truly matters.
We return to Sacrament. Breathe not a word of this meeting to anyone. Close our counsel’s ranks and purge the Guard of those with uncertain loyalties.
But you’re wrong. They all matter.
Baurus came a long way and at great risk to deliver that warning. Do you believe what he said?
I fear it. Is that enough?
So. The hunters say the old reservoir is the source of the trouble.
The way through the mill won’t be easy. It’s been abandoned for some time.
I’ve known some of those hunters a long time. Reed’s daughter used to play with Odessa when they were young.
The sound of children’s laughter seems... of another time, doesn’t it?
There’s always time for a good laugh.
I could smell the blood on your weapon before we saw you, Cerim. It seems you’ve been busy.
Keep up the good work.
Ho, Cerim. Welcome to our camp.
I wonder if you might have come across two of our party back in the Glades. Reed and his daughter Lara.
She’s likely dragged him into trouble again. If you see them, tell them they’re missed at camp.
Go on ahead. The hunters know these hills better than any. If there’s a way past this filth, they’ll have the answer.
See? I told you the Cerim would come. And here they are.
Indeed. Your presence is welcome here. My friend is convinced that some threat awaits us at the Weeping Sisters.
Perhaps if I had a clue as to our mission, I would not grip my sword as tightly.
The Cerim delivered a letter to me, passed from hand to hand. Unsigned, but stamped with the royal seal.
It said a place, a time, and three words - “Don’t trust her.”
But do you trust the sender?
We won’t know until we can get past this mire.
Cerim, it seems our route to the Sisters is flooded. There’s a hunter’s camp to the east; they’re gathering food for the Rites of the Fallen.
Perhaps they can help drain these channels.
Cerim! Did you hear it too? Sounded like cries for help. Trees being torn up by the roots.
Governor Ellsworth told me to stay here. He and Winnick followed the shouts toward our camp.
Please, help them.
The waters have drained, but the walkways within are rotted and unstable.
I was securing the path for Ellsworth and Winnick when we heard it...
Please hurry to our camp, Cerim. I fear my fellow hunters are in danger.
I swear this pass was clear last month.
Be on your guard, Cerim. Don't let the sunflowers and soft breezes fool you. It's blood that nourishes these hills.
I fear our hunt is futile. Most animals that drink these waters fall ill and die.
The ones that don’t take much more than arrows to bring down.
And when you do, the meat is... wrong. Like it’s already rotted inside their bodies.
I hope you’re able to drain the reservoir. For all our sakes.
We hunt for the Rites - that's reason enough.
Lost my brother to a Risen arrow four years ago this winter. Never even saw the archer.
Just one minute Cal was alive, and the next he was in the dirt. Like he was choking on air.
For a long time I'm ashamed to say all I wanted was to join him.
But the Rites of the Fallen, celebrating his name, his service, it brought me back.
That's why we do this. You grieve to keep from forgetting. But you honor to remember.
I know if I'd died instead, my brother would be out here, bringing down a boar in my name.
I could live off berries and nuts I suppose.
I'd offer food but we have none. The plague spoils our game.
Personally, I think it's a lesson from the almighty.
Every season I join the hunt for the Rites, and every season I wonder if there's a better way.
I know our quarry die so that we may live. But what do you see in a dying buck's eyes?
Me? I see fear, not purpose.
Are hunting and killing really so different?
Reed's no fool, there's something in this forest.
We find trampled trees and boars torn apart like paper dolls, but tell ourselves it's just a passing storm.
I know the Rites only come once a year, and the fallen deserve tribute, but not at the risk of joining them.
They want to make Sacrament proud, for this year's Rites to be a banquet. Pride, all pride.
The forest is full of hunters, and only some of them walk on two legs.
Watch yourself, Cerim. Something spooked my father, and he’s not one to scare easily.
With sickness in the reservoir and Savor in the mill, I’m glad this is your mission now and not his.
Don’t tell him I said this, but- I feel safer with him at my side.
I’ve hunted in these woods since I was a little girl. But it was never like this.
The governor’s daughter and I used to whittle swords out of saplings. We’d chase field mice, pretending they were wolves.
Now the wolves are real. And Odessa has... gone her own way.
Ho hooo! We both hunters, ain't we?
Come to join the fracas, have you?
Me, I'm gonna bag me a Torn wolf. That's right, you heard me. Put it right on me mantle.
Some here killin for food, killin for the Rites. I got a belly full and ceremony enough. I kill for the prize.
No sweeter stink than the blood caked in me hair. If not for the wife I'd never wash it off.
Don't lie - you got a ledger of your own, doncha? Carrying your trophy room with you between your ears.
A word to the wise. Seek your prey where others won't.
Follow your gut, it'll lead you to the kill, every time.

Who are you? 
You're not from Sacrament.
We don't need any more mouths round here! Haven't got enough supplies as it is.
I should never have signed up with this outfit...
The Hunt is just part of the job. I'm happy to serve.
Nomara, they call me. Because it's my name. Nomara.
I've said what I have to say. Now go stick your nose somewhere else.
Your business out in these woods is your business. And mine is mine.
Be careful, Cerim. There’s something far worse than Torn wolves and woodsmen out there.
I really did hear something out there, Cerim. At first I thought it was a bear but...
Then it roared. And it didn’t sound like a bear.
It sounded like... torment.
Lara says it was my imagination.
I hope she’s right, and the only thing that crosses your path is good fortune.
Oof! This ground is like stone.
I can't do it. My arms have gone to mud.
I'm not a feeble man. But we've been out here for three days with not but turnips and porridge.
And this dirt won't give. I can't even get my shovel in a thumb's length.
Just... pretend you never saw this. I'm pathetic, I am.

Yes, finally! That's the start it needed!
Thank you!
...Gods, I really am useless.
I.. I need to get back to Sacrament. I don't belong here. I'm not meant for this.
Thank you, stranger. I'll say a prayer to the Maker for you.
And please, don't tell anyone about this.
Oh my - a Cerim! That's unexpected.
You're just about the last thing I would expect to wander into our camp.
Are you staying in Sacrament?
My half sister's there. She's an enchanter. If you understand all that hokum, you're wiser than I.
In fact - I don't suppose...
No, never mind.
Thank you for delivering my letter. ...I don't know if I could look Eleanor in the eye to hand it over myself.
I... I'm embarrassed to ask this, but -
Would you give her a letter for me? My sister, I mean.
I keep meaning to deliver it myself. Yet we never... seem to cross paths.
Eleanor is her name. And Sora is mine.
...The truth is, I haven't spoken to her in quite some time.
If she seems angry, or annoyed when she reads it... Don't mind her. That's just how she is.
Sit still, father! I can’t tie the bandage with you squirming about.
Yes, and don’t forget barrels. The deadliest creature of all.
Is that a hooper’s knot? I’m not a trussed up goose, am I?
Ho, Cerim, welcome. I’m afraid we’re in a sorry state. Foul water chokes these woods, and the plague is rampant.
But at least my father is in one piece! ...He nearly lost his leg tripping over an old tree stump.
It was a barrel! And I was fighting for my life! Fending off those - things - that have taken over the old lumber mill.
If you’re trying to reach the Sisters, then your troubles are the same as ours.
There’s a reservoir past the old mill to the west. That’s where the filth is coming from.
My father tried to drain it - but something tells me you’ll have better luck than him, Cerim. Here, I’ll open the way...
It’s no mill, not anymore. It’s a Savor den, filled with deviants and monsters and -
These men need our care, but we’ll meet you at the Sisters once you’ve dispatched the beast.
My father used to take me hunting in these hills, and my grandfather used to take him...
I don’t think I’ll take my sons.
Cerim! The waters are draining but we heard… shouts from beyond the treeline. We —
Don’t go! You'll end up like the rest, torn to pieces! It’s got claws like iron and poison for blood!
So it bleeds.
I told you it weren’t no bear!
What happened? Where are the others?
There was... a beast...
It took my Lara…
It tore right through us.
I’m supposed to protect her. But I ran…
It’s not your fault.
Perhaps it is fate that you came after all, Cerim. So this carnage does not go unanswered.
I’m so sorry…
Return to their camp, and see if you can track the creature.
Winnick and I will tend to Reed and Ferrin here, before we continue to the Sisters.
Gods forgive me. I can still hear her screaming... like a ringing in my ears.
Of all God’s creatures, I never thought the Pestilence could defile the sigil of Sacrament itself.
How many... how many made it?
It was a bear. But it wasn’t.
Forgive me, I don’t know the word for... what I saw.
But the camp. Del, Sora, Mavlo.
And Lara. It took her. All of her.
I think Reed escaped. So did I. I was lucky... I got away... I was lucky...
The bear roared, Lara screamed... The bear screamed, Lara roared...
They'll sing songs about me…
Down there is where I taught Lara to swim...
She took to it like a fish to water - always was better than me at everything.
Each time, she pushed further and further from the shore... Till one day she went too far.
I had to swim harder and faster than I ever have in my life to bring her back.
I could swim out there again. But this time the waves wouldn’t be taking her from me.
Leave me, Cerim. You have much to do, and I’ve nowhere else to go.
Ah. There you are, Casper.
I see you’ve met my friend. Please, forgive us our guile, it was necessary.
Something in my gut told me something in yours would keep you from ignoring old Casper.
Don’t worry, I’ve not brought you here to ask for copper. Or Savor.
...In fact, I’ve something to give to you.
This letter needs to make its way to Ellsworth’s hands.
A little guard told me he’s in the War Room right now. I’ve got no shoes to my name, but they’ll let you walk right in.
What do you say?
I know what you’re thinking. What’s a worm like me doing with a message for the governor?
It’s not from me, you ox.
This island is a tapestry, my friend. And one little bit of string can go all the way from Beggar’s Alley, clear back to the mainland.
If you want to survive, you’d best start learning which strings around here are short. And which ones are very long indeed.
Quickly now. Mustn’t dally. If I know Ellsworth, he won’t linger in the War Room long. Not with Sacrament under threat on all sides.
Deliver that letter, so I can get paid. And my Casper can get his dinner.
Psst. Cerim. I’ve got something for you.
You don’t know me, Cerim, but I know all about you. I know you’ve got the Governor’s ear.
A little guard told me he’s in the War Room right now. I’ve got no shoes to my name, but they’ll let you walk right in.
Cerim. I... She was gone when you arrived. Do you understand?
Many of our affairs concern you. But not all.
A letter? Please, let me see it.
...The eyes of history indeed.
Winnick and I must make for the Weeping Sisters at once, south of Sacrament.
Hm... But the route through the Lowland Meadows is scarred with Pestilence.
Perhaps our interests align once again. Our protection, your glory.
An outstretched hand may belong to an enemy or an ally.
My burden is that I must shake the hand regardless.
This island is scattered with the ruins of those who thought they were eternal.
Every day I worry we’re one step closer to joining them.
I’ve known Odessa since she was just a baby in Annora’s arms.
And still, the number of guards who say to my face that she should hang...
Makes me wonder what they say about her behind my back.
So, you survived. Did you speak with Ellsworth?
Careful, Cerim. Ellsworth’s inside with Odessa. He had her summoned to the War Room this morning.
Even I’ve got the sense to steer clear of that.
If you venture into the War Room, I suggest you be discreet. Or well armored.
One final stone to unturn.
I thought perhaps Sacrament’s Guard, or Phalen’s faithful might...
I thought I wouldn’t be alone.
I have nowhere else to turn, Gods help me. Nowhere but...
I was once like you, young and strong and without fear. I will show Irmgard the man I was.
If I fail, so be it. But I refuse to outlive my own home.
They say he left already...
Excuse me, is it true that Governor Ellsworth has already gone north with that Madrigal?
The guard said as much, but I wasn’t sure - many doors in Sacrament stay shut to us Dasha.
I’d hoped for an audience. He has much on his shoulders, I know, but my home is... unwell.
Perhaps I can speak to the Orison. Yes, one man of faith to another.
I promised her - I promised them I wouldn’t return to Marin empty-handed.
So many stray cats and dogs wandering Sacrament. What they could teach us of loyalty and grace. I wish I could take them all home with me.
Why would the Seeker guide me here only to fail? Why would the Mother fill my heart only to break it?
Forgive me, I have slept little lately. And when I do, I dream of those piercing eyes, the awful Blight choking my home.
I wish there was more I could do.
I can offer a warm meal, a kind hand, a prayer. Beyond that, we must trust in the Embrace of God’s many hands.
I have no stewards of my own, and the Inquisition’s only concern on Sacra is rooting out the Pestilence.
But that’s the very same foulness that plagues our forest. We want the same thing.
I fear they... won’t see it that way.
Please. I know you see our faith as blasphemy but -
I hold no malice toward the Dasha. I’m not heartless, just... powerless.
Thank the gods I wasn't at the Gate...
Horror after horror... Is that all that awaits us?
I knew Caylen was lost when the quarry fell.
The only safe place left is this stinking city.
I never thought I'd consider myself lucky... but at least some of us made it out of the quarry.
From what I hear of the Mountain Gate... It was a massacre.
They say the sky turned black. They say people were swimming in blood!
Those poor souls would understand what I did. When the plague has you by the leg... you'll do anything to survive.
He ain't seen what I seen.
Pretty words won't hold them back. Nothing will.
They don't know... No one here knows...
I couldn't just set them free...
I can still hear their shackles rattling.
They were just criminals. Barely even men.
You've seen the quarry down the Nameless Pass. You understand what things are like there! I'm... I'm a survivor. I did what I had to do.
It was us against them. They were like animals! With the plague in their eyes, it was... It was terrifying. I couldn't think.
I'm not proud of what I did, no, but - well, if I hadn't, I wouldn't be here right now. I'd have ended up just like them.

I - I still see them when I close my eyes, their hands, reaching toward me -
 ...Anyway, what do you want?
Need to get me old seat back... I will, I will...
This crisp cool air is no good for me lungs.
Water? Pfft. Like I'm some puddle drinker.
Oy, traveler! Have you been to The Dusty Loom? I mean before she burned down? She was the finest tavern on Sacra.
Caroline's saving me table, I know. Just until she has enough copper to re-build her... Should be any day now.
Say, d'y like I can sing ye a song? It goes like this... Zzzzzzzzzz.
Ahhh, the wood remembers the shape of me arse.
No sweeter perfume than sweat, ale, and a hint of sick.
She's no tavern - she's a cathedral.
Didn't I tell you, traveler? Is she not resplendent? Is she not a tavern to make you drop to your knees, and weep?
I'd offer you a fresh pint, stranger, but I seem to have finished me one here, before me. Which means, I'll have to offer me a fresh one... for me.
I like you, traveler. I consider us friends now.
This city's gone to shit.
Better off sleeping under a doorway.
Where's the work ethic anymore?
The grapes gone sour! Hehe...
Hello. Are you looking for a place to live? Well you can't come here to me. All my properties are full, thank you.
I remember when Sacrament was a city on a hill. The beacon of the Ashen Sea! Now look at it. I'm almost ashamed to be a lord here.
When I bought my first property I was merely a child. All it takes is grit and savvy, my friend. Grit and savvy. And an ample inheritance.
Do you partake of ale, or wine? You strike me as the ale type. Pity. I've a fine Elgarth red sitting at home.
There'll be blood in the damn water soon enough...
Fish eat the dead, we eat the fish...
Thought we was sitting pretty on top of the food chain.
World's ending, and I'm spending my last days with the damn fish.
Least the wife stopped asking why I never fish outside Sacrament's walls.
Out there you're as likely to see an arm or a leg go bobbing by as a fish. No thanks.
Sometimes wish I was one of them. Glass-eyed moron, too stupid to be afraid. Nah, fuck fish.
Death swooping down from above. Suppose now I know how the damn fish feel.
Scaly bastards, always nibblin’, never bitin’.
A shit creek full of shit fish.
Look at 'em. Flashin' their little tails, blowin' their little bubbles. Fuckin' arseholes.
Ech, I'm useless. No wonder Sasha wants to leave me.
Better burn me when I die. I refuse to feed a one of 'em.
I fucking hate fish. But I can’t hunt for shit and I can’t farm, so here we are.
Once hauled up a fish with a drowned cat in its belly. Guess what was in the cat’s belly? ‘Nother fish. Hehe.
Some days they won’t even touch a lure or hook, but stick your toe in the water…
Wife says my breath always reeks of fish guts. But what's her excuse?
Please, spare a few coppers for those who’ve fallen on hard times.
Any bit will help, coins or crumbs.
Charity ain't some dirty word. It can feed our stomachs and your soul.
Everyone speaks of the suffering outside our walls, but ignores those of us suffering within them.
Even Ellsworth’s turned a blind eye to our corner of Sacrament. Just because we have nothing doesn’t mean we’re not people.
King Harol’s in the courtyard, going for a walk!
While the queen is in the kitchen, tasting the baker’s stock!
Prince Magnus hides in the stables, the lighting... it’s so dim!
But what is this... that I see? The horse is mounting him!
What’s the matter? You a Bolein? No sense of humor, eh?
Emma? Peter? Oh, I’m sorry. I have no sight and thought you were my children. They’re coming to get me today. Perhaps tomorrow…
Should gather my things. Be ready to go when they come to take me home...
A killer, eh? I can smell it on you. I was like you once -- tracked down Raiders and worse, for anyone who paid.
Under their breath they called me the Bloody Butcher... I confess I loved it.
Took a job once that led me deep into the Floodlands. I got the bastard too -- But not before he nicked me in the arm splashing about like a dying fish.
Didn’t think much of it at the time, but... that water... It wasn’t long before the black rot set in.
Lost my arm to no more than a pinprick, d’y believe that? And now I’m here. They don’t call me the Butcher no more... They don’t call me nothin’ .
Don’t think the same can’t happen to you, friend. We’re all someone in this world until we’re not.
Please traveler, help my baby. They say the sickness took her, but... but she’s still here!
She just needs food and a warm blanket. I know I can make her well again. My poor, sweet child...
She keeps crying...I can’t make her stop...
Spare any copper for a lonely old beggar?
If your pockets are weighing you down, friend, have some charity for old Casper here.
We’ve known each other a long time, he and I.
Something bothering you? Think I look familiar, is that it?
I’ve never met you before in my life, Cerim.
...At least, not until one of those long strings starts tugging again.
Then we’ll be oooold friends.
Spare some copper? Please. A coin couldn’t hurt you.
Welcome to our little corner of Sacrament.
Spare a moment, if not a coin.
We may not look like much, but everyone has a story...
Won't you meet my eye?
A wretched bunch we are, but a family of sorts. They’re all I’ve got anymore. Them, and old Casper here.
Lost it all to that cursed drug Savor…
Say, you wouldn’t have a drop or two of it on you, would you?
Just a drop of Savor. No one has to see.
Just a few coppers for an ale... I’m so thirsty!
You there... Please... Wait...
I can get back on my feet... I will, you'll see!
Coppers, please... I beg you. I can work, I’m good for it... Just need a bit of strength.
A warm ale to prop me up... Put the fire back in these bones. Please!
Curse the Dasha! God’s punishment will destroy all of Atlan.
His loyal children will die alongside these filthy Dasha heathens.
Curse them and cast them out!
Alms for the righteous! Death to the Dasha!
The massacre at the Gate is an opportunity for the rest of us.
Why leave it all to rust and ruin?
The Inquisition is slaughtered, the plunder is ours for the taking.
Mountain Gate's not a locked door no more, it's an invitation.
You know any men of stiff nerve and strong stomach who might seek their fortune at what's left of the Mountain Gate?
Bolein steel. Phalen's finery. Not to mention whatever the Inquisition plundered in God's name. All just lying there in the dirt.
Winged Brood might've picked the vanguard's bones clean, but what about their pockets and purses?
I hear the way to Caylen is piled with the bodies of holy men who died clawing at the Gate. Ruby and emerald rings still on their fingers...
Inquisition got their wish granted - to meet the Born God face to face. They've no longer any need for earthy possessions.
A mountain of ore just sitting there...
A fortune at our fingertips.
If you have to die for something, why not riches?
The quarry misses the song of her pickaxes.
Inquisition cleared the Torn out of the quarry. Or most of them anyway. Leaving what... lonely little rocks shining for no one?
All I need is a new pickaxe, a deep satchel, and maybe a partner to watch my back while I swing.
It's all a matter of perspective. You can say massacre, abandoned, corpse-riddled. Or you can say - opportunity. Which sounds better?
Took all that time digging the quarry, putting those cranes and gates in, seems a pity to let it go to waste from a little plague.
You look like the adventuring type...
I quite like the Governor's daughter. Not beholden to anyone. No fear, no hesitation. No husband.
Can you believe, my life's half gone and I've seen so little of my island, let alone the realm.
I've never glimpsed the mines of Tir, where the furnaces churn beneath the snowdrifts, nor the twin sister isles of Havenport.
I'd like to lay my hand on the Mountain Gate. Stare into the ancient eyes of those stone Cerim faces.
Here, can you place this one?
… That's one of my favorites.
… It just takes practice.
See if you can follow along.
A true Cerim! And in Sacrament of all places.
Should you find your way to Tir, Cerim, you'll be treated as royalty. We know how to properly revere blood.
I've a hint of Cerim blood too, you know. On my mother's side, eight generations back.
I can't imagine what brings you to a sty like Sacrament. In Tir we live among the clouds.
Ellsworth's a fool with his gates and guards. Ice and stone alone have kept Tir safe for a hundred generations.
I'm sure it's nothing.
She's never been gone so long...
This time feels different somehow.
Gods, I think I can smell myself.
My wife's vanished before. Many times I confess. But never this long.
I'm sure she's alright. Off somewhere thinking of me right now. Of my supper...
It couldn't possibly have anything to do with... those shadows in the sky. That shrieking from the east...
No. No, I'm sure she's just dallying with that trader from Marin again. That's all it is.
Excuse me, I must keep looking. Bola! Bola!
Bola! Bola!
Where's she off to now...
If a man can't be respected in his home, then he's no man at all.
Haven't we grown tired of this little game, darling?
Unremarkable height, dark dingy hair, poor teeth. If you see her, tell her that her loving husband misses her.
It's not natural, a man's wife being out of the house for this long. I'm long overdue for a bath, and who's to warm it?
She's always been the rambunctious, see-the-world sort. While I prefer the realms, eh, between the topsheet and the duvet.
Our home has everything she might need. Her stove. Her linens. Her washbasin. And her betrothed!
Rare specimens must be preserved!
Perhaps the human body itself is a grotesquerie.
Think of thorns as nature's handshake.
The brambles want only what we all want - to live.
Each one of God's creations is beautiful in its own way! Even if prickly. Or malodorous. Or... studded with twitching eyes.
Some indecent pillock has been trampling and slashing through the rare undergrowth in Marin Woods.
The Marin brambles are no doubt endangered. Perhaps one of a kind. One must treat them with delicacy and reverance.
I can assure you the brambles are more afraid of you than you of them. If they feel fear. Which I'm sure they don't.
Like I always say... Zealotry and prosperity never mix.
Used to be, the Church understood its purpose.
Expansion and influence, under the banner of God. That was its only goal.
This is why the great Lords, such as myself, have always supported the Church. Prosperity is the safest path to salvation!
But these... fanatics, and their reckless devotion are tearing up the contract.
What good did she think would come from destroying the Gate? What wealth is there to be found in a city of the dead?
I won't lose a single coin to that Madrigal's ambition, thank you. No, no. Not I.
Sacrament - such a dreary muddle.
Perhaps next time my manservant can come in my stead.
There's a certain stench to this city, don't you think?
Someone really ought to set this rabble straight.
Look at this place - the prosperous and the beggars living side by side? It's madness.
In Tir everyone knows their place. And when the lowers forget, the uppers are always ready to remind them.
We try to keep these trading ventures short. I fear if I stay too long I'll be infected by the... lowborn.
Seems almost criminal to trade away our silk and steel. But food is hard to come by in the Frozen Peaks.
Next round's on me!
I've got coin to spare, boys!
Fancy a charter? I'll sober up by the time we reach the port.
Too drunk to stand don't mean too drunk to row.
Big hooded fellow paid me a king's ransom to row him from his tallship to some cave beneath the Lowland Meadows.
Couldn't tell you why he didn't just dock in port, but I ain't the type to question easy coin.
Strange one, he was. Kept muttering about a storm coming, even with the waters flat as glass.
Made me take the long way round too, skirting Ship Graveyard, like he was searching the wreckage for something.
Anyway, think he wanted things kept, what's the word, clandestine. Lucky for him, these lips are welded shut.
Looking to rent a skiff, stranger? My fee's cheap, and I'm always discrete. Ask anyone.
This is interference in the free market.
I'm being punished for my enterprising spirit.
Please just move along, sir.
Sir, you can't just buy out all the vendors and then resell at twice the price.
Why not? It's my god given right of commerce.
We've barely got enough to go around without someone trying to profit off recent calamities.
This city has become a boot on the neck of any entrepreneur!
I demand an audience with your superior! I'll have you sacked!
Oh that would be a dream come true.
But with the Winged Brood loosed from the Gate, Randolph isn't letting anyone go.
Mother says trying times make strong men. I think she just wanted me eaten up.
Is that so? I confess my own mother could be quite... demanding.
Gone six years this month. A hateful, miserly woman. I miss her dreadfully.
Perhaps in these trying times your wealth could be better spent aiding those with less instead of striving for more?
If I wanted advice from a horse's ass, I'd strike up a conversation in the stables.
Of course the wine is corked...
Well, you know what they say, if you want to find a good meal on Sacra, go to Phalen.
I do appreciate this establishment opening its doors again. I'll admit it makes this city feel a drop less dreary.
I suspect the chef must have a new benefactor. A financier from the capital, no doubt. Perhaps he can introduce me.
What's a man got to do get served around here? I must've ordered that shepherd's pie an hour ago...!
Man can't make a livin' anymore.
It's a city, not a charity.
Never grateful for what they've got.
Who says everyone deserves a roof?
The more houses Maker Danos builds, the less I can charge for me own. Landlords gotta eat too, ya know!
If Ellsworth had any sense, he'd sweep beggar's alley clear. Those sorry sods drag down me property value!
All this charity toward the Dasha gotta come from someone's pockets. Consider mine sewn shut!
Sendin' aid to Marin, sendin' troops to Havenport - what's next? Takin' the food right out of my mouth?
So you're a coward, then! Simple as that.
Do you want a brave husband or a breathing one?
Mora, did you even see the thing?? It had six legs! And jaws like a... like a...
Like a what? So you're scared of an insect, is what you're saying?
It weren't an insect, it was taller than three men!
We've got no food on our shelves, Durgan! Our stocks are empty!
Do you want me to die? Is that it? You want rid of your own husband??
I want a husband who will provide for me! Who won't piss himself stinking at the thought of stepping outside the city!
There is food at the market. There are fish in the river. We have all we need here!
Well, you ain't getting what you need here until you go out and bring me back a proper roast.
Oh, now darling, come on…
Mainland ain't so bad.
Opportunities aplenty in Phalen I hear.
Never even seen Waithe or Eversol.
Vanguard's welcome to stay as long as they like.
What's the point of being part of an empire if you've only seen one corner of it?
Perhaps I spoke too soon about the King. About our King. Maybe I should visit Phalen, pay my respects.
Sacra will always live on in me. But does that mean I've got to always live on her?
I'll come home to Sacra. Eventually. Once this mess has sorted itself out.
I'll say what we're all thinking.
Old King, new King, same boot.
Sacra's fine on its own.
Hope those Bolein knights march right into the sea.
Thought you were one of them soldiers from Phalen at first. Another pair of dirty hands, to keep the King's clean.
New to Sacrament, eh? Look around. You see that, there in the mud? Boot prints from Phalen. They're all over this city.
Mainland thinks if they let us govern ourselves, the whole island will pack up and leave. That's why they keep Ellsworth on a short lead.
Everyone's too scared to say it, but Sacra and Phalen are better off apart. I love the King about as much as a wart on my eyeball.
One of the Governor's better speeches, I'll give him that.
Rousing words, but empty all the same.
Ellsworth speaks like he's one of us, like he cares about us.
But never forget, he was born royalty on the mainland. After our city is ashes, he can simply... go home.
Sacrament needs fresh blood in her veins.
Governor Godfrey - it just sounds... right.
Lend your voice to mine.
Do you see that? That glimmer on the horizon... You know what that is? A new dawn! That's what it is. A new dawn for Sacrament.
Ask anyone on the street. This city's in the gutter. We might as well be living in the Black Trench - who can tell the difference anymore!
Beset by raiders, Pestilence on the rise, outsiders buying up all our property... Sacrament's no place to live anymore.
Elra P. Godfrey, that's the name to remember. I'll be Governor of Sacrament before you know it. All I need is your help to spread the word.
You're not voting for me, you're voting for yourself.
Ellsworth's had his chance! This city deserves better!
Ellsworth let the Risen take the old Fortress. How long until he surrenders our very homes?
We're the crown's subjects, not its slaves.
Who's even in charge here - Governor Ellsworth or the Madrigal?
Ellsworth let the Inquisition march right over his back and through our streets.
Does Ellsworth care more about our needs or the Madrigal's wants?
One relic poking and prodding at another...
Why did Ellsworth scurry off to the Mountain Gate? Is he too scared to face the problems here at home?
Ellsworth and Winnick can't even stop a bunch of ragtag raiders and thieves.
When will Ellsworth deal with Darak once and for all?
My sources warn of an impending attack by the Risen from above! Yet our leaders do nothing.
I hear Ellsworth let Odessa slip free in the night.
The Governor released his own daughter! Corruption! Inequity!
A Risen rebel. An enemy to law and order. And he lets her walk right out the gates.
At least now we truly know where Ellsworth's loyalties lie. And it's not with us.
What if the plague comes next for your home, your mind?
First the quarry decimated, now Marin Village nearly lost. What's next?
Elect Elra P. Godfrey! Before Ellsworth sends our fair city crumbling into the sea, or worse!
Where is Ellsworth when we need him most?
We need a leader, not an empty chair!
While Ellsworth visits the Hunter's Vale for sport and game hunting, the rest of us struggle and starve!
I've concluded I can contribute most outside the public eye.
I've decided to temporarily suspend my campaign!
In these turbulent times we should look for steady, unchanging leadership.
Governor Ellsworth, we thank you for your service, and look forward to you surmounting these challenges.
With the recent... events regarding the Mountain Gate, I think it's best if I spend more time with my family.
I've never seen such a spectacle. She pointed a sword right at the Madrigal, can you believe it?
So she's left this world at last, then?
Ha! If it were you or I, she surely would have. But this is the governor's daughter... She's probably taking a warm bath right now.
And you think Dorrick and me are mad for wanting to leave this place...
Where else would we go? Havenport? Ha! I prefer to keep all ten fingers, meself.
How can any of us trust Ellsworth? Our soldiers fall to the Risen, while his own blood blows air in their bellows!
Where were you then? Everyone in town could hear her shouting!
Sear my feet, I was at the river - collecting dinner! You know Dorrick's still injured...
Odessa may be mad, but she's no leader. She's just a lost child.
Aye, on that we agree.
What do you mean, gone?
Word is, she's no longer inside Sacrament's walls. Could be she escaped. Could be Ellsworth let her go.
That's family for you. Dorrick's cousin once chopped off two of Dorrick's toes. Still have him over for supper.
Dorrick's cousin ain't setting fire to mainland ships!
He might if he was smart enough to tell which side of a torch is up.
That girl needs a mother, that's all I'm saying.
She's got one - ain't you been to the cemetery lately?
Well Odessa might just join her if she keeps picking fights with the whole of the Atlan Empire.
Don't tell me, I missed it again?!
Not much to miss - I heard she's gone.
If I ever get locked up, will you spring me?
Ha, if you're ever in a cage, you know i'll be in the one beside you.
We oughta do this more often, you know. Let Dorrick and Warren fend for themselves, while we dine like ladies!
Sure, sounds grand, if either one of us were made of silver.
Mighty kind of old Gordon to give us a discount on the soup! He's all right, that one.
Shhh, we musn't talk too loudly, he told us Caroline would scold him if word gets out!
Say, have you seen that new one wandering about? The one everyone's gossiping after?
Yeeeeahhh, some kinda mystical holy warrior, they say! Imagine that! ...No, I haven't seen 'em.
S'pose we really did it though? Just ran off together? Catch a boat to Phalen, or Bayscathe?
Oh come on, don't start that again.
Ain't this place looking divine? I forgot we used to have nice things in Sacrament.
I can't remember when we ever did!
I've got a new pet.
Rufus, where are you?
Where's he flown off to now?
He gets so hungry...
Rufus doesn't have Zalamaya's pretty purple stripes, but he has such lovely big black wings. And teeth - so many teeth!
I tried introducing Zalamaya to Rufus but... it's my fault, I I should have fed Rufus dinner first.
Rufus stays mostly in my head. But his brothers and sisters don't, and they miss him oh so much.
He's a hungry little piggy! Always flying about looking for more food. And such a messy eater too.
Zalamaya, come here...! Where are you?
Sneaky little bandit.
Who am I to play with now?
Maybe she's hiding in last night's dream?
Have you seen her? She's such a pest, always wandering off. Please, keep your eyes out!
She's a fine cat, when she stays in my head. But sometimes she just gets up and leaves, and I can't find her anywhere!
I'm looking for Zalamaya, that's her name. At least, that's her name this week. Next week, she might be Tillimuntanto!
Zalamaya, she's a big orange fluffy creature. With purple stripes. And, I think, maybe antlers? What do you think?
If it needs doing, I'll do it.
Feeling squeamish? S'alright, it happens. You need a man with a strong stomach, and no morals. That's me.
There's no lock I can't nibble loose. No window I can't wriggle through. Got this city wrapped around my finger, I have.
I've seen how they look at you. Yeah. Like you just stepped over their mum. We're outcasts, you and me. Misunderstood.
Once you understand that laws around here are more like... suggestions... your whole world opens up. Life is yours for the taking!
I hear there's a fortune under our feet.
Little birdie tells me the Trench is piled high with some new long-term residents, breathing and otherwise.
A right ransom in loot just waiting to be lifted off necks and out of pockets.
Not my place to ask how it happened. Forest critters don't question the corpse they're picking clean.
But if you find anything shiny amid the sludge, save some thanks for yours truly, won't you?
So it's done then?
A few volunteers returned to the Vale to bury the dead. They said they never found Lara's body.
Might sound strange but I don't hate the beast. The plague hollowed it out, left only pain and fear. I'm glad it's at rest.
We were supposed to gather game for the Rites to honor our fallen. Instead we just grew their ranks.
If you see Reed, tell him to come home.
He never returned from the Lowlands. I think he's still searching for something of his daughter to bury.
We hunt the forest. The Pestilence hunts us. You hunt the Pestilence. What hunts you, Cerim?
Never wanted to see him like that...
You think you know the plague? Are you the one who will save us all?
You don't know what the Pestilence is. You're a child, playing in the sand. Making up stories.
Have you looked into the eyes of your beloved... as his face turned inside out, and his eyes were pulled down into his throat?
I've seen what the plague does. I've watched it take everything I've ever loved. And then crack its flesh open... and smile at me.
He was a man. They all were...
You hacked your way to our gates without a moment's thought.
Our hero, everyone, our hero has come!
Butchering their way through what's left of our friends, our family, our children.
No, I'm afraid I don't know.
You don't know?
I've no idea!
If I had to guess, I would say ox leather - but it seems like really you're the expert.
Oh, nonsense!
I thought you said you were an expert.
I said I studied to be a tailor, that doesn't mean I know every type of fabric in the world.
But you really can't tell me whether this is ox leather, or – Oh. Hello.
Why, it's you!
Do you know each other?
Er, we met once, yes. It seems you never know where this Cerim might turn up.
I've met them before as well. Isn't that strange?
Cerim, please allow me to introduce – Petra, isn't it?
Yes, that's right. And you're Giles.
I am indeed. You see, we've only just met. Petra –
I stumbled, like a fool, and spilled my drink on him. It was horribly embarrassing.
It was barely a splash. And anyway, now we're having a fine conversation. All's well that ends well.
Anyway, it was nice seeing you again, Cerim.
Yes, lovely to see you.
Oh, why do I do this to myself...
Huh? Why are you talking to me? No, I'm... I'm a mess. Believe me, it's not interesting.
My friends want to meet at The Dusty Loom for drinks. Do you know it? Caroline's inn, I mean.
But I can't be bothered going out. I... I'm not feeling well. And it's so loud in there.
I think I'll just... go home and sleep instead. Yes, that's what I should do.
I just... need to go lie down.
What would be the point of going out anyway? Probably just have some drunk spill their beer on me.
I don't know why you keep talking to me. My mind's made up. I don't even like ale anyway.
Please, just leave me be. I'm not going.
All right. I suppose I could go for just one drink. You've badgered me enough. Let's get it over with.
I'll go to the tavern, just for one drink.
Oh. It's you. My only companion, it seems.
My friends who invited me here didn't even show up. Now I'm just... a man, sitting alone in the corner. Story of my life.
I appreciate what you were trying to do, but - now do you see? It was pointless to come here.
Oh well, I guess I might as well have one more pint.
Not even sure there'll be a next season.
Blood ain't much of a compost. It's the iron in it.
I hearby order you to resume your duties. Please?
We have to eat. I have to eat.
The Governor has ordered all food production be increased.
What, just keep my gaze upon the soil with that Winged Brood circling overhead?
We can't keep you safe if you don't keep us fed.
I could grow a tomato out of a tar pit, but you can't fatten up a corpse.
Won't be no carrot and onion stew this season. No stuffed goose. No rabbit shanks with roast cherries.
Oh Gods, my stomach.
841, the year Sacrament became a graveyard.
Not a good year...
Might as well be tilling cobblestones.
Wish God's hands would reach down and help me with this bloody work...!
Seasons come, and seasons go. But bad luck is eternal.
Don't expect these crops to yield much more 'n turnips. Maaaybe the radishes'll pull through. Shite year all around though.
822, the ground was fair bursting with produce. I made more copper at the market that year than in the three before it!
835, we had a crop of blackbirds nested in those cliffs below the Rookery. Hundreds of 'em! They covered every inch of my farm in stinking shit.
836, that's when my Harriet passed away. How I miss her. (sighs) ...Ha! It's not true. The shrew left me for a merchant sailor.
Last year was better than this. But still shite. I had one pumpkin out of fourteen survive. Would you believe that?
833, now that was a good year. Rained just right. And the gophers were all over at Farmer Korel's, hehe. I made a mince pie that year!
825, interesting year. Back when I first moved to Sacrament... No rain for four months, could barely get a hoe in the ground.
Six years ago we had a storm come through that just about flushed this whole damned city to the sea. There is such a thing as too much rain, don't forget it.
Back in 816, I had never even touched a spade. I was a young peacock - I wanted to fight in the arenas! Aye, I was tough as nails then.
827, not a year to remember. The spring was sticky, the summer was hot, and I was drunk for most of the winter. Hehehe.
A few years ago I was out in this very field, and do you know what my hoe pulled up? A chamber pot! Heh! Looked like it had been in the ground since before Bilsgard.
824, you know, that's the year Annora Bolein died... I don't think the governor's ever been the same.
If you make for the Glades, be sure you have what you need.
A thin, green line separating us from the Risen. That's what's outside this gate. A thin, swampy, stinking green line.
Promise me - anything that comes through this gate, you'll help me fight it off. Won't you?
Only a fool would leave Sacrament's walls behind without a full stock of food and a freshly sharpened blade.
The Orban Glades used to be a fine place to cast a line and pass the day. At least, that's what my father used to say. Before he drowned.
You heard the Governor, head to the Rookery.
Make sure to get a good scrub in after wading through the Glades.
Wouldn't want to end up all rotted away like them Nith.
And is that sand on your legs? Came all the way from the Shallows in this weather?
Can't say if you're brave or just foolhardy - but you won't catch me being either.
The Rookery sits above the town square. Just follow the signs.
The gate to the Lowland Meadows is closed. A foul beast has been seen roaming outside the walls.
None may pass.
Do you know where you're going? The Meadows aren't what they used to be.
After the farmers fled, used to be the wolves had the run of the place. But now... There's something else.

I wouldn't head south unless you're looking for a swift end. Or you're fearsome stubborn.

You want to see real filth, visit Sacrament's sewers. 100 years of shit and rot and decay, sloshin' about like in a tub.
You get used to the stench. You even start to miss it after a bath.
Hmm, something's off... Can you smell it too?
It's coming from the Trench. Stench wafting up out the sewer pipes.
More than just your flu shit, your pox shit, your bad fish shit. Smells like death. Like bodies. Lot of 'em.
Can't smell it, eh? Of course you can't. Heh, ain't got the nose for it.
Oh well, paid to scrape shit, not study it. Unless it comes oozing up through the grates, it ain't my concern.
A Cerim? What a joke.
The Pestilence is already among us, Unspoken. You've come too late.
Where were you when the Torn first began to stalk us? Where were you when it would have made a difference?
This city is at war, make no mistake. Ellsworth doesn't know it yet, but I do. The only safety left is a blade in its sheath.
We should just open the gates and let them pour in. See who's standing on top of the pile when the blood dries.
I remember visiting Caylen, before it fell...
That Gate has always been a black mark on this island.
Hm. The Cerim's still alive. That's interesting.
Never felt a city so on edge...
If there's one thing I've learned in all my travels... wherever the Inquisition goes, ruin tends to follow.
I've toured many splendid cities and lost ruins, but with Caylen I never thought I'd see one become the other before my eyes.
You know, there are no Cerim relics in Myrfall or Waithe. No monsters in the sky either. Just... drawing a parallel.
Perhaps it's time to explore one of Sacra's neighboring isles. Which one? Well... whichever has the soonest boat departing.
Smaller every year... This city keeps shrinking.
I must pay a visit to Havenport before I leave the island.
Poor Sacra. Always scraping by on the Empire's crumbs...
I've probably traveled farther than anyone in this city.
My word. A Cerim. What ship did you arrive on? There haven't been Cerim on Sacra in... Dear me.
My name is Jovison Corinth, explorer by trade and by passion. I've touched every corner of our Empire.
Fascinating, fascinating. I've never come across a flesh and blood Cerim. Did you come from Tilos, by chance?
Maybe your kind live in The Seethe now... That's as far as I've been. What lies beyond the black sands, my maps do not know.
There! The Cerim! Heresy in our midst! Their sin darkens our skies!
You see? The sickness fills the very air above our heads! This is what your sins have brought!
It's only a matter of time before the Pestilence is inside our walls... in our streets... our homes!
Forgive me God for occupying the same ground as such a heathen, for breathing the same air.
The Madrigal brings salvation to our sickened island!
We must show the Inquisition our fealty! Kneel before them as they pass!
The mainland shines its light upon us at last. Soon the Pestilence will flee back to the darkness whence it came!
Do not ask why the Inquisition has come. Ask yourself if you are worthy of the Embrace!
God will curse us for saving the unholy village of Marin!
We should let the Dasha rot in the swamps and forests outside our walls! They are where they belong!
The sickness in the Marin woods will soon find its way to our city! We must close the northern gates!
We should have left the Dasha's minds to rot, the way their souls already have.
The pagan gate will fall and Caylen's faithful will be saved!
God has sent the Madrigal to fulfill a great purpose... The holy city will soon be free!
Praise the Inquisition - God's many hands are at work in the Nameless Pass!
The holy city and her many wait for us, trapped behind heresy like the sun behind the clouds.
The beast outside our gates is a sign of the blasphemy within our walls!
We must accept God's embrace, or we will all end up like that wretched thing!
The evil that stalks our island will not be defeated with swords and bows! Only God's hands can save us!
The Pestilence is a punishment from god!
The Pestilence is a punishment from god!
The righteous need not fear the Pestilence! It has returned to cleanse the world of wickedness and sin!
The Dasha blasphemers bring the plague upon themselves! They refuse to abandon their ancient, primitive faith!
The Mother, Maker, Seeker, and Forsaken? Heresy! There is only one god, and we are all cradled in his many arms!
There is smoke on the wind and thunder in the distance - God's righteous fury has arrived!
Oy! You! I saw that! Too frightened to look me in the eye, eh??
Whoa! How dare you rush a man like that, weapon at the ready - do you want to die?!
Bah - I'll have you know I've bested seven men in mortal combat. And many beasts as well. Large ones! Like bear-sized!
I don't like you, and you don't like me. I hope we meet in Boroth's arena one day – so I can wipe that smirk off your face.

I'd fight you here in the open, but the guards... 
Well, they know my face. And my reputation! My unmatched reputation!
Don't like the look of you...
Who are you? Whatever you're selling, I'm not interested. Go on, run! Back to whatever cave you crawled out of.
Look at 'em all. Peasants and thieves... Not an honorable soul in the whole city. I oughta leave this place.
Got cut loose by old Boroth. Would you believe that? Yeah, I used to work there. Cleaned the arena. Preening prick. Good riddance!
Sheesh, your breath stinks. Why don't you turn your head the other way?
And who might you be?
Hello there. Have we met before? You've certainly got a way about you. Let me guess – you're a trader. No, an explorer!
Isn't this a fine town? There's no place I'd rather be than Sacrament - where all the good people come together.
Care to have a seat? A tipple to make your mind right? Go on, why in such a hurry? I won't bite.

At least Sacrament has a good man at its helm.
What happens in this city can ripple all the way up to our little village of Marin.
That's why I'm grateful the governor is a thoughtful man.
He might be a Bolein, but... he has the heart of a Dasha.
Sacrament's too noisy to sleep, too crowded to breathe.
You can't even hear the trees around here...
I should get back to Marin soon.
Everyone's always in a rush...
I don't care what others say - Ellsworth's a good man. He doesn't treat us Dasha like mud to be scraped off a boot.
I come from Marin, just north of here. Brave the woods once a month to trade what we got for what we need.
Mainland church only has one god - can you believe that? How's one god alone supposed to look after all this?
I'll say a prayer for you, traveler, at the Sovann Circle; so the Mother, Maker, Seeker, and Forsaken can all hear.
I don't hear it roaring anymore...
They say you killed the creature outside the gates. You don't see monsters like that in Marin.
This city's got a pull to it, like it draws in all the island. The good and the wicked.
I only stay as long as I need to. But with those foul brambles in the Marin Woods, it's been hard getting home.
I thought Marin was safe.
I didn't know how bad the woods had gotten.
The Temple of the Seeker, it's... It was always a place of peace.
I'm here trading apples and cloth like a fool, while my family was nearly lost to the call of the plague.
I should've been there. Not that I could've helped, but it's where I belong. If Marin falls, so should I.
My Igney wrote saying she's safe, but told me not to come home. Not until she's certain the danger's passed.
There's no price on my head!
I heard rumor of what you did to those other deserters in the Nameless Pass.

Please, cowardice isn't a crime. Or it shouldn't be...
I've heard words like those before.

And for what? Mud and stale fishcakes and killing poor fishermen who took up arms against Phalen.
What were they fighting for? Probably someone else's rousing speech.
I'll earn my keep.
I was never meant for a uniform.
Maybe more opportunity here than Phalen.
I ain't dying for someone else's sigil.
Sacrament welcomes all, isn't that what they say? It's what they say on the mainland, anyway.

What's my business? I plan to lead a long and prosperous life. Right here, inside these walls.
You! Ohh... A horrible death awaits you. It trails you like a shadow…
I know your secrets, the ones you keep even from yourself...
Only two people know why you came to Sacrament. You and I...
Your truth will not come easily, nor cheaply...
Dark deeds swirl around you, stranger. I can see them. I have the gift of insight, and outsight... Do you wish to know more?
Morietta the Touch, that's my name. I know what awaits you. But the secrets of the Unspoken Realm are not given freely.

I see you in a high place, and a very low one...
Yes, you will venture to a deep dark realm of filth and grime... and make a new friend.
And you will climb to dizzying heights, and the world will open up to you.
A vision! You walk among the treetops and rolling hills.
I see you in a land of predator and prey, comforting a gentle woodland creature

I see a Cerim...

Think you got one!
Nah, it's just a bit of sewage.
Who's that? What are you doing! Can't you see I'm concentrating!
But I'd have a belly full of fish, wouldn't I?
God's reach, that's a Cerim, Murgos. Look at it.
A what? A syrup?

Never heard of 'em, don't care. All I see is an ugly sod frightening the fishes.

The whole bloody place is their territory! I swear, you'd be dead five times over it weren't for me.
Ship graveyard... They’d be feeding you to the fish sooner than you’d be catching any...

You can't still think that.

It's that Darak. They say he drives them like a wildfire.
Ellsworth should've burned Lion's Mound to the ground when he had the chance.
Ellsworth's not a warlord, he's a politician.
Ha! And look where that's got him. Now they're scratching at our door.
I heard Odel was on the bridge when it happened. Poor bastard.
Aye, Sacrament lost a lot of good soldiers out there.
If they ever breach our walls, I'll go down swinging, mark my words.
Need to pack my bags... Get out while I still can.
Mabel says she heard from Hala that you two are making for Phalen. That can't be true, can it?
If Ellsworth wants to lead a hopeless war against the plague itself, he can do it without my help.
Come on now, friend, don't be hasty. We've weathered worse.
Have we? There are demons in the sky, Neville.
It's a fine mess, I'll give you that.
So why don't we go toast our doom at the tavern?
This is no jest. Hala and I are leaving. And you and Mabel should do the same.
But... who will I argue with?
Where did I leave my damned boots?
Should have never have let the Risen take the Keep...
Don't worry, my friend. The Pestilence will get us first!
Where'd you tell Hala you're off to today? Mabel thinks I'm splitting firewood.
That's it! The Pestilence is taking me...
