Hold your breath around me! It's in my legs right now... But it's working its way up. Only a matter of time.
Are you feeling ill, stranger?
There may be no stopping this scourge.
It's spreading like a flood...
I fear Caylen lost to the sickness, but I haven't given up hope for the rest of our fair isle.
If my patients want the comfort of a prayer, who am I to deny them such frivolities?
I've never seen symptoms like it, and I can discern no pattern to its spread, but I do what I can to ease their pain.
I can't say I buy into all this mystical claptrap, but there's certainly a plague afoot.
Were you just in Marin, traveler?
I hear a strange form of the sickness took hold there. A sort of mass psychosis.
Perhaps I shall visit, see if I can be of service. And hopefully dispel some of these superstitious rumors.
I don't understand it.
There is still evil here...
I should have come sooner.
There's no rhyme nor reason to why some have recovered and others appear in a fugue.
They speak of voices. Of "him." They sway in place or wander into the Woods. And they simply... waste away.
I refuse to concede - I won't leave this village until I've healed them.
The gods have left us, if they ever even existed.
Our own Mender was powerless against him...
There's no beauty left in the Marin Woods.
I doubt I'll be any safer here in Sacrament.
The Pestilence brought Marin to its knees, and where was the Mother? The Maker? The Seeker?
If I don't believe, then I'm not Dasha. And if I'm not Dasha, I have no place in Marin Village.
I realize now how foolish I was, praying to a circle of stones. The rocks aren't listening.
If there is a god, it's the Forsaken alone, calling us to our end. The others are just children's stories.
The church welcomes all, traveler.
Is that...? It can't be... A Cerim, in Sacrament!
Welcome, welcome. I'm the Orison here. Orison Haley.
God speaks in countless voices, and I am but one of his humblest.
Try not to be intimidated by those Inquisitors marching around. The Church is a place of peace.
It is when we are still that we are most likely to feel God's hands upon our shoulder.
Strange as it is to say, this island made a better man of me. I hope it will do the same for you.
We are all but the hands of the one true God.
And yet... it is your kind who are said to share one mind, one soul, between you. I believe you call it the Untold, yes?
All the world spoken into being by your Sayer, with our silences and shouts watched over by the Cerim.
A lovely sentiment. And who knows - perhaps we are all servants of the same being, if only under a different name.
This house is a trifle compared to the great cathedral in Phalen... Or the one in Caylen, for that matter!
But still, this is God's den here in Sacrament, his embrace made manifest.
The mainland might frown upon me welcoming Dasha into these walls, but what is salvation without those worth saving?
They're good people, kind and generous, even in the face of generations of suffering.
And their Mender in Marin - Irmgard - is a wise woman with a sharp tongue. Have you met her?
Oy, Cerim! This is your fault! You did this!
They’ve shut me down! Run me out on the street! All thanks to you and your ilk.
I’m Sacrament's stonemason, just like my father, and his before him. That’s my shop over there, through the cemetery.
But now, BAH! ... Shuttered. Disgraced. The whole place beset by leeches!
...and now I’m shut down on Ellsworth’s orders! He’s got some academic rooting around, claiming it’s a “site of interest.”
Pfft, site of interest! All your kind ever did was not wipe out the Pestilence!
You better fix this, Cerim. Or I will.
Soldiers dying on the daily, and who will remember them? There’ll be an unmarked grave soon enough.
They’re your ruins. Go tell that dormouse to leave them be.
I'll never meet anyone...
Oh. Excuse me. Don't mind me. I'm sorry.
Oh, why do you keep pestering me?
I suppose I could stop by, just for a minute. But only so you'll leave me alone.
You don't want to talk to me. No one ever wants to talk to me.
There was a time when I thought I might meet someone, here in Sacrament, but... Well, I mostly just stay home now.
I was going to head to the Dusty Loom, but - what's the point? I'll just go home instead.
It's loud there, and it smells. Yes, I'm better off at home.
I said there's no point in going to the tavern. I'll just stay in.
I... I don't know why you're still talking to me.
I don't want to go out. I'm all right on my own.
Please, just leave me be. I'm not going.
All right, I'll go to the tavern. But I don't know why.
Hello again. Yes, I'm here, look. Does it make you feel smug?
This place is just as hopeless as I remember. The only ones who come here are drunks. And it smells like sawdust.
Oh, why did I listen to you? What did I think was going to happen?
I guess I might as well have one more pint.
I can't stop shaking...
My skin feels electric.
Do you know what it means to be alive?
The sky... They were everywhere...
I grabbed everything I could and ran for Sacrament's walls. Gods, my heart still hasn't stopped racing.
Those things, swooping down from above, people screaming. I felt so... alive. I mean, I wanted to live.
They're asking for volunteers to venture out, gather supplies that were left behind. Maybe I should...
The fear... it's like a color that I never saw before this moment. Is this what battle feels like, Cerim?
They killed Pavos, they killed Lurina. And yet everything tastes better, sounds sharper, feels more real.
Stay back! I'll not be pulled into the void today.
I won't let your occult dabblings put my life at hazard.
Keep a wide berth, Cerim.
You're not just Unspoken - you're unwanted.
Charming! Some find it charming - the way you rip apart the world, then put it back again. Charming.
I know the workings of your kind. Speaking what should remain unsaid, whispering at the edges of our world. It's unnatural.
How many of you have there been? A hundred? A thousand? Your life ends, your story finished. Yet you speak yourself anew. This is not what God intended.
More and more of them, I've heard them. Ever since you set foot on Sacra. The Whispers – gashes in the sanctity of our world.
Mm-mmm-mm... And the leaves... upon the wind... Mm-mmm... Never more... Mm-hmm, again...
Hello, traveler. Yes, you may look upon my work. But it is not finished yet. It is never finished.
Inspiration is like water... Snaking its way across the dirt. It knows not where it goes, but where it goes is always right.
I used to paint in the woods outside the city's walls. The Marin forest... What a place, what a haven of beauty.
It's safer to paint inside the city now... No deviant fowl here. No feathered men. No... None at all...
ohhhhhh, I didn't ask for any.... maybe tomorrow.... ohhhh
Not fit for the dogs... We had two of them...
Look at it, just look at it! There! Hiding under my skin. Between my bones...
Please... water... no, not to drink... just to, to...
I've been here before... I've done this before... But YOU weren't here...
I don't think she's well...
Listen, friend - think you could get the guards to move my cage a bit farther from Ava?
I did what I did, and I'll pay for it, but I don't need to be catching whatever she's got.
Can't even sleep – she's up all night moaning about... well if you understand it, you're wiser than I.
Put a sword in my hand and put me on the wall. Rather die there than puking my guts out.
You're the one in a cage, mate. Not me.
No banquets in Lion's Mound, no castles to hide inside either. But we're free. Can you say the same?
Mainland puts a leash around your neck and you think you're something special? You're a dog, that's all.
Ellsworth, Elias Graftston, the Lords of Tir - just puppets of the king. Hang 'em all.
Revolutions are fed by blood. If that's to be my own, so be it.
Just need a few more copper and a few more men.
I'll be damned if they bury me on Sacra.
How soon am I setting sail? Yesterday.
The doom from the Mountain Gate will cover this whole island soon.
I'm putting together a crew to sail off this god forsaken rock. I'll take beasts of the deep over demons in the sky any day.
I've got a lead on a skiff, might do the trick.  But I'd sail a rusty bucket if it took me away from here.
All are welcome to join me in fleeing this cursed port, save you, Cerim. I'd sooner put to sea with a Nith Leviathan than you again.
North to the Yawning Isles. West to Thorn and The Shattered Hand. Or South to Kylesh - anywhere the air ain't filled with the shrieking plague.
It can't be...
Of course you lived.
Of all the islands to be wrecked upon.
Take you and your luck elsewhere, Cerim.
How did you survive the wreck? I thought I was the only one, and I clung to a piece of driftwood for three days.
Some of these people act like you're a hero. They'll learn soon enough - you're a curse.
Lotta good men died to bring you to this island. And some not so good. But you owe all of them a debt.
I told the captain to steer clear of Sacra. Now he's dead and I'm stuck here. At least the ale's cheap.
Did you hear? Risen bastards who sank our ship were led by the Governor's daughter. As if I didn't hate this place enough already.
I can see you're liable to make a name for yourself on this island. Killed a few of the Torn, have you? Hm. You have no idea what war is.
A blade and fancy armor do not make a warrior. You, my friend, need to learn patience. Cunning. And most importantly - when to retreat.
Want to learn something? Always watch your enemies carefully. Study their attacks. Their aggression is your opportunity.
Have you ever been stabbed, Cerim? Felt the cold plunge of steel inside your ribcage? I have. And I'll tell you... I'd like to feel it again.
My expertise is demons of the conceptual variety.
If you can't see it and can't touch it, I can stop it.
Sometimes we must face our nightmares alone.
Before you ask, no, I'm not equipped to perform a seance for those loved ones lost to the Winged Brood.
And no, I cannot dispel the creatures themselves, for they are corporeal beings and I specialize in the spiritual realm.
And finally, no, I am not in a position to offer refunds on home exorcisms if your home has subsequently been destroyed.
But if you are plagued by, perhaps, the ghost of a child. Or a small dog. Then I am at your service.
I am a humble soldier in the war against apparitions and phantasms. Other threats are others' business.
Notice anything unusual at home?
Open drawers and misplaced cups, perhaps?
Rodents aren't the only infestation.
Sometimes a voice in the dark is exactly that.
Congratulations, you're a property owner! Got yourself four walls and a roof, eh? Sure, there's nothing like the safe haven of home.
But I must ask - and you'll forgive my prying - did anyone tell you about the history of the place? ...Before you paid?
And have you perhaps noticed anything... odd... since you moved in? Say, a piece of furniture not quite where you left it?
Look, I don't want to alarm you, but - there's a dark past to this city. And there's a dark past to your home.
That's why you're lucky you met me! The name's Raven Cranning - I'm the only spirit hunter in Sacrament with a perfect record.
…In fact, I'm the only spirit hunter in Sacrament.
You keep an eye out at home, and if you see anything off... You just come and find me.
I can help you rid your home of specters, wraiths, shadows, and wisps - for a small fee, of course.
- Was plenty sharp enough to fell an elk across the river!
It was really more of a creek.
Betrayed by my own flesh and blood. I’ll feed you to the next wolf I see.
Oh so I’m safe then.
Don't mind my friend here. He's harmless. Unless feathers make you sneeze, ha!
I'm Reese and he's, well, I just call him Squawk. For obvious reasons.
He used to be Balak Taw. At least until he gave up the Great Nest for ale and my stellar company.
Yes yes, and to stop the bloodshed. Dunno if he's any good at being a pacifist, but he's a pretty good drinking friend.
It was just a joke. I've known chickens with a better sense of humor.
God's reach, you got feathers in my drink, you drunken sop.
Don't go ruffling at me! Looks more like a mating dance anyway.
No no no, it's your turn to pay. I know you got pockets somewhere under those feathers.
You'll never believe it.
Soaked to the bone, I was.
Really makes a man think.
Nothing like flirting with death to make you cherish life.
I was minding my own business, scavenging for crabs on the coast...
Find me a nice girl in Havenport or Tir. Perhaps that was God's message.
And VHOOM!
Felt like a whole ocean of putrid water came crashing down on my head. Lucky I didn't swallow any!
Washed away my nets, my satchel, everything! Nearly swept me out to sea.
By the time I found my footing, it was just a foul trickle down the rocks.
Ocean was still, not a cloud in the sky. Where did it come from??
Have I offended God? Not let my hands be part of his many?
Maybe it's a sign - deluge washing away my livelihood and all - to devote myself to God.
Or maybe... it's a sign to let my wife and boy think I drowned. Start over.
Fistful of the ocean pouring out the sky - I sound like a madman.
I told you! Don't say I didn't!
Rest of you finally learning what I already knew.
Sacra ain't an island, it's a graveyard.
Think you're safe behind them walls? Ha.
This damn island already took my leg. Now it's back for the rest of me.
I learned long ago, same thing's behind every locked door, closed gate, and sealed tomb - your end.
Seems your Cerim Gate was about as useless as you are. Don't know why I expected any different.
I used to want to see the whole Empire. Now I just wanna see my next sunrise.
The island will chew you up and spit you out...
You ain't seen what I've seen.
Better off right here in Sacrament.
Think tonight will be a cold one...
Come to gaze upon my misery, have you? Feast your eyes upon my festering misfortune?

It was frostbite took my legs! In the Frozen Peaks, beyond the dead ships. Venture there and you'll meet your doom, I promise.
I went to scour the ruins to the east... The realm of the ancient Cerim. Nothing but death in those mountains now.
Here I was thinking things couldn't get any worse.
Getting more than a bit crowded behind these walls.
Guess the Inquisition was praying to the wrong god...
There's such a thing as too many customers.
My cousin was from Caylen. Last time we spoke she said I had rocks in my head. Least I still got one.
I can mend a tear, scrub out a bloodstain, but I need 'em alive to pay the bill.
You know how I know my husband ain't no monster? Because he'd never whisk me off my feet.
I told Bavos ain't no need to fish outside Sacrament's walls. We can make do off potatoes for awhile. I hope that clod is staying safe...
Do you mind? Got work to do. Real work.
Wish these bleedin' peddlers would close up shop once in a while. Can't hear meself think.
Must be nice prancing around the island all day. Some of us work for a living, you know.
Don't think anything will ever get these bloodstains out...
Is it true your kind worships a Sayer? I do most of the talking in my household - think my husband worships me?
Do I look like I care who sits upon a throne a thousand miles away? Rest of us just scratchin' out a livin' down here in the mud.
Imagine, bunch of grown men killing each other just to be a footnote in some scholar’s book.
Far as I'm concerned, all this just boils down to shit stains and bloodstains. More work for me.
So, you're the one who killed poor old Warrick.
Used to be a man, you know. I'm friendly with his widow, horrible bitch named Sigrid.
Just her luck. Husband runs off to join the Risen, gets turned into a monster and then killed by a Cerim.
I can't even get mine to choke to death on his supper.
Strangest thing...
Am I going mad?
I've made that trip countless times before...
Back in Sacrament... How did I get here?
I was on my way to Marin Village to sell my apples and turnips... and next I knew they were rotten in my satchel. Every last one.
I don't think I ever made it to Marin. I must've gotten turned around in the woods. But for how long?
My wife said she thought I left her! But I was only in Marin for an afternoon. Wasn't I? I feel all turned about.
Have you ever been to the Dasha temple in Marin Woods? I haven't. Well hadn't. And then I was. Sorry, I'm not making sense.
The hands inside your mind...
Ours is the Born God.
Only the final God matters, not the first.
Our body is a debt.
Every person in this city is a husk, and the fruit from which they were shed was God. We must let him inside of us again.
The Pestilence is not the end of your story... It is the path that will lead you to the Many Hands. It is a great blessing.
I will speak with every man, woman, and babe in this city. And my words will slip into their minds like fingers sliding through hair...
There is room in God's embrace even for you, Speaker of the Dead. His hands can penetrate the darkness inside you.
Don't think I know you.
Keep walking stranger.
I've no quarrel with you.
Just please, keep it to yourself.
If I had any dreams of shrugging off the Atlan Empire, well they died down in the Sewers along with everyone else.
I've just a familiar face. I get it all the time.
Is it the smell? Was a damn fool earlier and fell into a creek, that's all.
Still trying to scrub the stench out.
Plague doesn't care if we were free or not, Risen or not, Phalen or Sacra. I could've been King Harol for all it mattered.
I said I don't know you!
Sacrament is my home. Always has been. You're the stranger, not me.
Just leave me be!
When I sleep I still hear the creaking of the Sewer pipes, the drip of filth, Darak's howls.
Darak was a madman, alright. I don't know why it took the Trench for me to see it.
Talo boosted me up on a high pipe. But when I reached down for his hand... it was too late. I crouched there all night.
You don't know who I am - you know who I was. No sense getting a man hung over someone who's already gone.
Oh, I just wish I had the chance to prove myself.
Would a decent war be too much to hope for? Oh to be conscripted...
I'd set sail and take the fight to the Risen in Lion's Mound, if not for my dreadful seasickness.
You know, the Pestilence should count itself lucky it hasn't breached our gates, or it would have me to contend with!
I think I'll head out into the Glades and cut down a few plagued monstrosities. Tomorrow perhaps.
I hear you beat me to the monster outside our gates.
Felled old Warrick before I could, eh?
That beast in the Orban Glades was supposed to be mine, you know.
I was fetching my armor when I pulled a muscle. Important to limber up before battle.
The quarry's grown quite treacherous, hasn't it?
The Nameless Pass is absolutely crawling with the plague...
The only way to reach the Mountain Gate is by blood and courage!
Or so I've heard. Haven't had the time yet to venture out there myself.
Leave some Risen in the Glades for the rest of us!
And to think, some people call him a warlord...
The Falstead would never have gotten away on my watch!
I hear you sent Darak scrambling. If he shows his head again, he'll have to contend with the likes of us!
Need a helping hand in Marin Village?
I reckon I'm just the savior those Dasha are looking for.
I'll head north, and drive the plague out of the Marin Woods...
Oh, already safe you say? My fault for not speaking up sooner. Perhaps I'm too courteous a warrior.
Those poor hunters in the Vale...
I heard that Ellsworth and Winnick had a brush with the plague in the Meadows!
That hunting party never stood a chance without us there...
I would've been with them, maybe even turned the tide, but they left before I could find my blasted bow.
We must be brave, Cerim!
Look to the sky, my friend.
This is the hour when we stand strong together!
The time has come to stand tall and prove ourselves! We each have our role to play.
You take on those winged beasts. I'll guard the sheltering women and children.
Do not fear, Cerim. I'm right here with you. Behind you.
That's beside the point. We're talking about great works.
Yes, so Kafron Bilsgard built Sacrament, I understand. But that doesn't change the fact that the Dasha settled Sacra first.
The Dasha were thieves and nomads, they found an empty island and they dropped anchor. Where's the surprise in that?
I'm not saying there's a surprise, I'm simply saying, whether or not they built a castle, Sacra belongs to them.
Poppycock, don't make me laugh! The only thing that belongs to the Dasha is three gods too many, and a bag of sticks.
And the only thing that belongs to Phalen is the extra hand up your bum!
That's blasphemy, you know!
Sod off, you knob!
And now we've got ghouls in the air... No good deed goes unpunished, eh?
Who? The Madrigal? If you think she knocked down that Gate for anyone other than herself, I got a king's crown to sell you.
So all of Caylen just written off with a wave of your hand? Now who's playing God?
They say the path beyond the Gate is ankle deep in bones. Not bodies - bones. Caylen's been gone a long while.
Well maybe if Ellsworth had acted sooner, they'd still be alive.
And maybe if my ass had wheels I'd roll home. Let's worry less about the dead and more about not joining them.
Aye, sometimes even you stumble onto a piece of wisdom, my friend.
So what now? Think the Madrigal heads home to Phalen with her tail between her legs?
She doesn't strike me as the sort to leave things unfinished.
So, God has finally embraced Sacrament, eh?
You know, my cousin joined the Inquisition last year.
Did he? Which one - Morrin?
No, Bernard! He says his whole life before was nothing but a shadow. Can you believe that?
God's reach, that sounds cheery.
To be honest, he's become a dreadful bore.
I don't mind these fanatics marching around the city. Just so long as they stay out of our heads.
Why, what would they find in yours? A dusty breeze?
No no no, I won't stand for that.
What's gotten your breeches all in a twist? I'm just saying, this city's a shambles.
That may be so, but it don't warrant you besmirching Ellsworth like that.
Giving one rousing speech ain't the same as being a leader, and you know it.
God knows what princely life that man forsook to live amongst us. And look at what it cost him - ain't he earned our respect?
We've all lost people we love, we've all been kicked down and shat on! That's just life on Sacra.
Then he really is one of us, isn't he?
Ellsworth may act like you could roll him over in his sleep. But if you ask me, I think he's a bear in winter.
Yes, but the Dasha were here first.
I pray to the Almighty no one ever hears the stupid shit we say, my friend.
Horatio's words ring true. How am I to believe in the legends of old if I don't believe in God's grace?
It feels as though I lived all my life in darkness, and the horrors at the Gate are like the spark of a candle.
Even the Inquisition's faith was not strong enough. I must learn to believe with every fiber of my being.
He's right, Cerim - it's not too late. We can repent and be redeemed. I will try, and you should do the same.
Did you hear that? Did everyone hear that?
Look at that! There, can you see on my skin? Gooseflesh.
I've never felt so many things at once! Inspired, worried, frightened... What an incredible moment.
I'm glad Ellsworth is here with us. If I were in his position, I wouldn't have the slightest idea what to do!
Maybe they know...
What a curious outfit! I wonder where they're going.
I have so many questions...
Hang on. Where was I headed?
Your kind come from over the horizon, don't they? Have you seen the Far Lands with your own eyes?
I heard there are giants in Giranoth. Real giants, that scrape the treetops with their fingers. That can't be true, can it?
Have you seen the sand ships of the far north? The falling deserts beyond The Seethe? Please, I must know if they're real.
Personally, I believe all the legends are true. And you're the walking testament! Er - may I touch you, please?
Caylen... it's gone. All of it.
Don't head north, traveler.
The holy city has fallen.
My skin still crawls with it.
I ventured through the Mountain Gate, fool that I am. Whatever I expected to find... it was worse.
The air is noxious, the city dark and half sunk into the Blood Lake. The Great Cathedral looks more like a ruin.
The city is dead. But not empty. Shapes and shadows move through the streets. Chittering noises. Teeth and wings.
Listen to me - the holy city is lost. Nothing will bring it back. Only thing we can do is bury it or burn it down.
Maybe I'm not Dasha after all?
Oh, why did I come to this city...?
All this faith is giving me a headache.
When I learned I was Dasha, I moved to Sacra to get in touch with my roots. I forgot that roots live in dirt.
Rise at dawn, work the fields, home with family in the evening. A simple life. And a boring one too.
What if that historian just misread my family tree? And it was a mistake to leave the mainland.
I don't need four gods. I'm not sure I even need one.
You don't look from around here. S'okay, neither am I.
So this is the jewel of Sacra. Heh.
Make a fortune in Sacrament, piss it away in Havenport.
I miss home, but she don't miss me!
If you ask me, we've been better off ever since Elias had West Havenport sealed away. Nothing but a soggy slum.
They say the Silverfish is responsible for every drop of Savor in Sacra. Never touch the stuff myself.
Ahh Havenport ain't so nasty. We just get a bad rap 'cuz all the crime. And drugs. And slums. And gangs.
Nothing compares to the view from high atop Havenport's great wall. Just don't take one step too many, eh?
Do you need any help?
I can sew. Patch your clothes. I can clean - or cook - or help you carry things! I know my way around the city. Please, just a moment.
My husband fell when the Risen took the old Keep. It's just me now... But I, I'm quite capable! I can even speak a bit of Dasha.
You've met Baron Winnick? Perhaps he could use a new servant? I'll work for just a few coppers, I will.
I... I feel as if I'm at the end of a terribly long bit of string. Dangling from the end, and... watching it fray.
Don't know how we'll survive now...
All those farmers not safe behind our walls...
I weep for them. And all those untilled fields, carrots and greens rotting where they lay.
Am I the only one smelling it?
Awful stench from the Sewers lately.
Must be what I'm feeding my boys. Worse what goes in, worse comes out.
This market wouldn't last a week without those Dasha traders...
Marin Woods all birdmen and brambles?
I suppose that means more rotten fruit and cornmeal full of feather.
Maybe those chaps from Phalen will sort things out...
Did the mainlanders get the quarry back on its feet?
Just pushed right through? Bah. I guess more cold meals without coal for the fire.
I miss visiting the Lowland Meadows. Used to be lovely country.
I heard about those poor hunters...
Do you think the ones who escaped brought any meat back with them?
Hmm, what's next on the list?
I fill the pantry, the boys empty it out.
I'm sure I'm forgetting something...
Ever since the Mountain Gate fell, some provisions have been hard to find. Whole island's being carved to pieces.
Does this mushroom seem off to you? I swear it's giving me a dirty look.
If you're one of them mainland missionaries, I ain't got time. I'm here to find apples, not god.
Ply your children with sweets and your wife with wine, and they tend not to judge your cooking.
Keep my chin up... Yes, and... eyes forward!
Do you know any of Sacrament's guards, by chance? I think they'd like to meet me. I have a lot to offer.
I came here on a ship from the mainland. Not as a passenger, mind you - I rode with the goats below decks. But I didn't mind a bit!
I heard you met Ellsworth. People say a lot of things about him, but - I think he's the best leader in the whole realm.
One day I'll be up on that wall, scanning the horizon, protecting the city! And maybe... I'll even get to shake the governor's hand.
I was wrong...
I saw some of the bodies brought back from the Mountain Gate. Or what was left of them...
I don't know if I want to be a guard anymore. I never imagined it like this.
It's not a uniform, it's a target. And the walls of Sacrament might as well be a feeding trough.
Those winged beasts - one crashed against the ramparts. It had a face. I think it used to be a person.
Huh? What? 'm busy. Move along.
Sweepin' here!
Can't you see you're in my way?
What the hell is your problem? Some of us work for a livin' y'know.
Rock never depreciates... Piss poor advice.
If you're looking to invest, don't come to me. Yes, I used to be a sage of commerce.
There'll be more silver in your sword than in my coffer now... Ever since the damned quarry fell.
People will always need ore and stone, my father said. He didn't count on those cowards sealing the Mountain Gate shut...
When Caylen was sealed, my business crumbled. Crumbled! You hear? Yes, I know, lives were lost. But that's not my concern!
Would you consider signing over to me, Cerim, the rights to your remains?
In case of death or dismemberment by those winged creatures, we wouldn't want your corpse to go to waste.
What glorious putridity coats your heels, Cerim? I must acquire some of my own.
Think of the rancid concoction I could brew. A bomb, a poison. Perhaps an ale?
So you've felt the caress of the brambles of Marin Woods?
Poor creatures. The ravenous are always misunderstood.
You know I chipped two knives trying to scrape off a sample of the Mountain Gate.
A most curious substance. Hard as steel, pitted as stone, and with a faint taste of old blood.
I heard rumors of a beast and maiden woven together in the Vale.
In my youth I often tried stitching crows and rats together, with limited success.
So what do you think, Cerim? A humble arrangement, but perhaps the start of something grand.
Yes, yes, soon even the birds will envy my plumage. My concoctions will haunt the dreams of the lustful, the weary, the spurned.
And you. Of course. You're always welcome to sup strength and wisdom from my elixirs. If they don't blind you, that is.
I can see behind your eyes.
Don't touch anything!
So... You're looking to be transformed.
I found the most curious fungus growing in the tavern's bathroom. I scraped up a sample if you care to see.
I'll never understand the sober. The body is a workshop - meant for tinkering. Why take only what you have, when you can have it all?
They say it's dishonorable to poison a man. If I could bottle honor, I wouldn't sell it.
Be silent as a whisper or loud as a thunderclap.
A man with untainted blood is a man unfulfilled.
Not all weapons end in a point.
Poison is just another word for overindulgence.
The most flammable stall in all of Sacrament!
The criminal, heretical, and unethical all under one roof.
Do you see? My stall blossoms, my creativity blooms. And what's to my benefit is also to yours!
I'm still not ready to admit you're deserving of my talents, but I do think I may be close to starting to consider the possibility.
Your gift is a blessing, Cerim. And now I might brew that blessing into a curse upon your enemies.
What’s this - our prize returns! Her stains a bit fresher.
Was the wearer dead when you found him, Cerim? No matter!
The world is brutish and cruel. True justice only exists inside the pit.
I declare the arena open to friends and foes alike!
Come, Cerim, and test your battle prowess in Sacrament's pit of war!
What fool told you that you were born between your mother's legs? You're born here. In the arena!
Your first steps a lunge with a lance! Your first words a battle cry!
But the one true game cannot resume without our prize: the Champion’s Crest.
Our current champion was last seen in the Nameless Pass, west of the quarry.
He owns the crest, until it is stained by his own blood. Bring him back, so that he might bleed for you in the arena!
The pit’s reward is pain and glory, not pain alone!
I ever tell you of the time I got my boot stuck in a bandit's skull? Ha, it's a funny story, trust me.
In a way I'm not so different from the vendors up above. Only I buy blood and bone, and I sell glory eternal.
What better way to make friends and meet strangers than by swinging at them with an axe!
You may be the stuff of legend, Cerim, but here you're just another bag of meat for the grinder. Least until you prove otherwise.
Find our champion in the Nameless Pass, so that the games may resume.
The arena's appetites are never satisfied.
Bodies become dust, but your name can live forever!
Are you a legend or a children's story, Cerim?
Death only comes for the ones who fear her!
I don't know if I'm grateful you're here with us in these dark times, Cerim.
Or if you're just another sign the times are getting darker.
Smithing's got a smell to it, no doubt about that. Not something most people enjoy, I've found.
But that's nothing compared to the stench on you right now! If I didn't know better I'd think you've been tromping around in the Black Trench.
A fine deed you did for those people up in Marin. You know my cousin Dolan's the village smithy...
If you can count the blind hammerings of that ingrate as smithing.
You've got some hardened feet under you, my friend.
When we first met, I never would have guessed you'd make it all the way to the Mountain Gate! And back again, alive!
Used to get most of my metals from the quarry through the pass. Haven't gotten anything out of there in a while now.
I've always made blades for the people of Sacrament. Her butchers, her soldiers, her hunters...
But it used to be, the blades would always come back with their owners.
Now... There've been too many lost in the Vale. We should look for game elsewhere, if you ask me.
Good to be back behind Sacrament's walls. My thanks for clearing the way.
From now on, how 'bout I stay at my forge and leave the heroics to you?
Good day to you.
Ahh... The savior returns.
Hello old friend.
I come from a family of smithies. My father says we're born with soot already under our nails.
Sometimes I wish I could be manning the battlements. But no, my place is here. I shape the spear, you drive it home.
Some people ask how I can stand the ringing in my ears. Better than hearing folks gab if you ask me.
Got some ore there, eh? You can buy weapons and armor from me, but you’re also welcome to craft your own.
Just refine your ore in the furnace, then use the anvil to shape your steel. You can smith anything you’ve found the designs for.
Most of Sacrament's vendors will let you do the same - buy something, or craft it yourself.
Nothing sings like steel.
Warrior's only as good as his weapon.
May your will be half as strong as my work.
Man's best friend is a blade.
I see the glint of steel in your eyes.
Victory is born in the forge.
Many thanks, Cerim. A furnace fit for a king! Or at least one that could cook a king, heh.
I wish my father could see what this place has become. So I could rub his face in it.
Just imagine the weapons I can forge now. It'll make the gods themselves hide in the clouds.
Rotten boards. Decayed and crumbling. Just like the old man’s mind...
It’s that apprentice of his... Useless scrapper. Couldn’t lift anything heavier than a pen.
And how can he think with that hat full of wax? I should have a word with Ellsworth...
Hmph. Who’s that? Oh, a visitor. Of course.
I’ve told the Watcher this tower’s not fit for livestock. And yet there he goes, boarding any stranger that comes along, when there are plenty of houses in Sacrament for purchase.
You'll have to head upstairs. There's no way down for now.
A fine staircase she’d be too. Would get us to the market in half the time.
Most days you'll find me not far from there. In the square, by the War Room.
Maker Danos. I can repair anything with the right materials, except laziness.
This city can be re-built! There was greatness here once.
Though it seems I’m the only one who remembers.
Find me down in the town square. I’ve wasted enough time with you here.
Let's get to work.
Where've you been?
Time ticks ever forward…
Kafron Bilsgard built this city from the wastes, and it's stood for 300 years. We must preserve his legacy!
Some of the ruins on this island were built by your kind... Many ages ago. I won't go near them – fearsome unnatural, they are.
Havenport, Tir, Caylen... There isn't a city on Sacra that isn't a shadow of its former self. Time eats at this island like mold.
We're not just repairing wood and iron, you and I. We're giving this city new life. Restoration is rebirth. Understand?
Wouldn't you like to see Sacrament reborn?
This island will be healed, one stone at a time.
They walk past, blind to the crumbling around them...
The blight of time is all around us.
We can restore history, you and I.
This city deserves a new beginning.
So, you found me. Perhaps you're developing a fondness for this city, then!
With my hands and your copper, we can make Sacrament bloom again.
Anything you come across that looks like it could be restored... Tell me. Why, even the vendors' stalls can be improved!
And for yourself - perhaps you may want a home here one day.
You can find vacant houses for sale all over Sacrament. Each one has a sign out front that tells you all you need to know.
There was greatness here once. Let us uncover it from beneath the dust.
I take it you saw the Madrigal from Phalen arrive. What a magnificent creature she is.
It's about time the mainland brought some rigor and respect to our shores. Too many godless boors around here if you ask me.
The word around the market is that the Madrigal summoned you personally to the Nameless Pass?
Is that true? You must command a mighty respect, to have been called upon by the Church. I tip my hat to you.
Are you sure you want to be running errands for that schemer Winnick?
He's got no honor, that one. Left his family in disgrace, did you know that?
It's true. He abandoned his own city, and now he means to drive Sacrament to ruin. I know it.
Heard you went north to visit the den of the Dasha.
I'm not surprised at what you found there - after all, they bring it on themselves. They're a cursed people, simple as that.
Been to the Lowland Meadows, have you? Did you know I used to own a house out there?
Yes, it's true. A lovely little cottage. I used to till the fields at sunrise, and watch the sunflowers bobbing in the wind.
But when the Pestilence came, I... Well, that's how you find me here! Right where I belong, in the heart of Sacra!
I remember when the plague first re-appeared on this island, Cerim. I've seen more death and decay than you might think.
Do you know what we must do, when horrors fill the sky and the weak run in circles like lambs?
We build, Cerim. We build.
So you've met that insolent historian Elsa, have you?
Be careful with that one, Cerim. She hasn't a lick of respect for this city. If it was up to her she'd rip up every cobblestone just to see what bones lie beneath it.
Daily drills. Marches. Inspections. Mock combat. Patrols. I'd like to think I prepared my men for what lies ahead.
But perhaps it wasn't enough. Perhaps it was never enough.
Think you're up for chasing down a few bounties, Cerim?
I told Ellsworth I thought it was a mistake letting you past our gates. A soldier with no rank is a stone's throw from a bandit.
But orders are orders. Or is that a foreign idea to you? Orders, discipline, training?
Well, as long as you're here, perhaps you might learn a thing or two by serving my Guard. You can start by showing your Captain a bit of respect, with a proper salute.
Every day it seems there's more. No rest for those of us keeping chaos at bay. What do you say?
It's my duty to keep Sacrament safe, from threats both inside and out. Don't test me, Cerim
You've seen Boroth and his silly arena? Real men and women don't fight for sport.
I was born standing stiff as a board, and I haven't given an inch since.
Do it for God and kingdom!
Beat a path of order through the chaos!
Better this world, one body at a time.
Maybe it's time you trade in that silly outfit for a uniform.
Why kill men for free when you can be paid to do it?
The ocean wants in, Cerim, and we are the wall.
Your true armor is your will.
Sacrament endures.
If not us then who, Cerim.
You call that a salute? Pathetic. I call it insubordination!
What in the foul reaches was that? I warn you, stranger - vulgarity has no place in Sacrament.
A jester, are you? My patience is shorter than my blade, Cerim.
If you want to serve my Guard, I need to know that you can give your Captain a proper salute.
Very good. Perhaps you're not quite the miscreant you appear to be.
Well then, Cerim - I've bounties to collect, challenges to complete, and not enough men to carry them out. Every day it seems there's more.
If you help me keep chaos at bay, you may find Sacrament's Guard can be a potent ally. What do you say?
God’s reach, what now?
My inn’s nothing but cinders. But no, that ain’t enough suffering to put on these shoulders.
Now I gotta deal with some outsider trampling over my livelihood.
Can you rebuild my tavern? No?
In that case, we got doors on all sides now. Kindly choose one.
Troublemaker, that’s what you are. Like them Dasha, or the Governor’s daughter.
Why can’t the lot of you just be civil? One god, one king, simple as that.
My Gordon’s a simple man. Knows his way around the kitchen and nowhere else.
I told him, go and fetch us a load of clams from the coast, down by the old Keep. Simple, ay?
Knowing him, he probably got carried out with the tide!
First the tavern, then my husband...
So, you're a Cerim, eh? Don't know much about your kind, but I know you're not from around here.
...As long as you're not Dasha, you're welcome in my inn. Or what's left of it anyway.
I've been trying to get that Maker Danos to help me repair it for weeks! But everyone in this city's bloody useless.
Oh well. I suppose you're no different than the rest. At least my Gordon's got a nice soft belly for me to rest my head on.
I wish I could offer you a bed for the night, Cerim. But until this place is re-built you're better off elsewhere, even under the Rookery.
This used to be the finest tavern in Sacrament...
You haven't seen my Gordon? Big man, belly laugh, mustache more crumbs than hair?
He's never been gone this long before... And the Shallows these days aren't as safe as they used to be.
So, would you like a bed for the night then?
Upstairs I've got everything from goose down to a sack of hay. You choose which one you want to put your head on.
The nicer the bed, the more copper it costs.
My Gordon found his way home, no thanks to you.
Other husbands wander in stinking of cheap perfume. Mine comes home smelling of cheese and jam.
Still, I wouldn't trade him for the world. He's making a pork mortrew tonight!
Ale below, beds above!
Dear me, you look like you could use a rest.
Bloodshed and turmoil, ha! All anyone needs is just a good night's sleep.
Seems like all of Sacrament's a ruin lately. This city's falling apart. That's Ellsworth for you.
Ah, I've missed the sound of footsteps in here. Pint glasses thunking on tables. I even missed the loud, flatulent drunks, God help me.
Back in my day everyone in this city was born here. Now you've got Dasha, mainlanders, Risen, those thieves from Havenport... And whoever you are.
God's reach, this place almost looks itself again. I can hear the fizzing of ale already. And... the thud of drunks falling off their chairs.
Well, I'll be! Look at this place! Maybe you do have a touch of the Embrace after all. Thank you, stranger.
Well I... I never thought I'd see the day. The inn looks as fine as the first morning my Gordon and I opened her doors.
Those beasts that poured out of the Gate... well, you go looking for trouble and that's what you'll find.
Gods reach, I'm starting to sound like Caroline!
You know I met Darak once. Fed him a bowl of soup half the size of a tub.
At least I think it was Darak. Big man, one leg, shock of white hair?
Just between you and me, I'm glad to hear the Dasha in Marin are alright.
They eat well and they keep to themselves. But if you tell my wife I said that, I'll deny it!
Weren't able to roll back the Mountain Gate? A pity.
The pie I could bake with the apples from Caylen's orchards... Say thanks you don't know, else you'd be crying yourself to sleep.
Some lovely words from the Governor.
But you can't farm words, can't stew 'em, can't eat 'em. They're a garnish.
I heard about the hunters. Terrible thing. And now I gotta scrape together a feast for the Rites with morsels and scraps.
I do what I can. But there are only so many ways you can dress up a beet.
Oh, it’s you again! My thanks, friend, for keeping our little “adventure” between us.
Cerim, eh? You know my wife thinks you're some heathen troublemaker. Like the Dasha.
But you don't seem so bad to me. Just another empty belly wishing it was filled.
Could hear your stomach growling before I could even see you.
Take your pick - it's all good.
Healthful and fresh. More or less.
The secret to a good meal? A bit of love, a bit of patience, and enough butter to kill a horse.
I stink of meat, my wife of ale. And our bedroom smells like a stew! Haha.
My wife Caroline runs the inn. She keeps me warm, I keep her fat. It's true love.
Not a war was won on an empty stomach!
Don't pretend you don't smell it. Come have a taste!
Every meal a feast!
You look a might peckish to me.
A full belly's worth more than a full purse.
A good meal's on your lips a moment, but on your mind for years.
You have my thanks, traveler. Any more time stranded up here and I’d be eating my shoes.
Wife’s gonna kill me. Think I’ll keep this between us, if that’s alright with you.
I know Caroline sees me as the heroic sort. Wouldn’t want to dispel her of that notion.
Oh I’ll clamber over the bridge. But not with you watching! That particular show won’t have an audience.
I’m up on top of the old bridge!
God’s reach, finally someone heard!
I was out fishing for clams when a pack of the Risen came through.
I thought I could make my way across the old bridge and out the other side of Mariner's Keep.
But this fort’s in worse shape than I am! The boards rotted out behind me, and the ladder ahead is pulled up.
Last time I try to be clever!
Please, see if you can find another way around before I end up like that poor sod over there.
Kick down the ladder!
You can make that jump, but I’d need to drop a few decades and a few stone to do so.
Can you find a way around? Don’t want to end up another corpse. I came here to fish crabs, not feed them!
Blast, you forgot to drop the ladder for me! Now you’ll have to go back around.
Not much smarter than I am, are you?
Ah! Finally! Some space to move around. Or perhaps to take a fine nap.
Things are looking quite shiny and swift around here, aren't they? What's next, me losing weight? Ha!
You flatter me, stranger. I... I never had such fine things as this. I thank you.
Help! Up here!
I’m up on top of the old bridge!
Damn bandits got me cornered up here! They took the key somewhere!
Help me, you fool!
And so it falls to us, to know the darkness that our mothers and their mothers and theirs did not.
Chosen or cursed, it does not matter. Let us prove we are up to the task.
My half sister Sora was among the hunters killed in the Vale.
We had not talked in quite some time.
I can speak a hundred encantations. Speak fire into stone. Speak ice into steel.
But I cannot speak to her. Not anymore.
What's that? A letter from Sora? Please, give it to me.
Is that... Sora's letter? Please, give it to me.
Of course, Sora. I always will.
Thank you, Cerim. Here, it's not much but - take this.
A letter from Sora? Pfft, keep it. If she wants to speak with me so bad she can do it herself.
We are all soldiers now, in the one true war. The one my mother and her mother and hers spoke of in whispers.
A black door was opened a thousand years ago. Perhaps together we can close it.
Greetings, warrior.
I felt the aura of your approach. And I saw you coming, ha.
Life and death in the balance. Let's tip the scales, shall we?
My mother was an enchanter, and hers before. We pass on what we can, but it's like carrying sand. Some always slips away.
I'll say a prayer for you to the Mother, Maker, Seeker, and Forsaken at the Sovann Circle. And another in the mainland's church. Times like these, we can't be picky with our gods.
I may not worship your Sayer, but sometimes, deep in an enchantment, I confess I can almost hear the hushed whispers behind the silence.
Why cut and slice when you can burn and freeze?
Make the world your weapon.
May your true name never be spoken, Cerim.
The stars align and my fortunes improve. Thank you for the upgrade, Cerim, I won't let it go to waste.
The Great Plague'll be shaking in its boots when it sees what I can craft now.
Can you feel it? The crackle and spark of new energy? My channels run deeper than ever.
Oh my goodness. Goodness me. Do I bow? Keep my eyes down? I've never met a Cerim.
I'm Farmer the Willem. Willem the Farmer! Not that you need to remember that. Or me.
I came down here to harvest the most lovely filth. Perfect compost. Honest, take a whiff!
But when I heard the Risen barreling in, I holed up here.
Not sure why you came all this way for the likes of me, but thanks for clearing a way out. I’ll make haste back to Sacrament. Please, find me there!
You came back? I mean, you came back.
You don't have to visit out of pity, you know.
What's mine is yours, what that there is.
My toes in the dirt and the stars as my roof - only a greedy man would ask for any more.
Back in Waithe, my father could till a field, my grandfather a forest. Here I can barely keep this patch alive.
I don't know much, but I know a pinch of black earth down the back of the throat cures anything worth curing.
Buy here... or not I suppose.
A bounty beneath your feet!
The soil speaks, you need only listen.
Cerim! I... Hello. Thank you again, for noticing me in the Trench. And saving me.
And... stopping to speak with me just now. You’re the first person who’s noticed I’m back.
Oh, bless the gods!
Strangest sounds in these Sewers. Noises through the pipes sound like growling, hissing, wailing.
Nearly soiled myself more than once. Didn’t need to come all the way down here if I was just planning to make my own compost!
Oh my. Oh my. I... don't deserve this.
I've never seen such fine things! I don't even know what to do with them.
I shall be forever in your debt, Cerim. I will name my son after you. If I... ever have a son.
The Gate falls. Caylen burns. What do we care?
The field of battle has grown. Nothing more.
You are stained with the blood of the Risen. They are fools, fighting for freedom.
They do not see - the fight itself is freedom.
You faced the Balak Taw? They learn well from the falcon's talons. But - like a falcon - their vision is narrow.
Every beast of the field has its lessons to teach us.
You have been to the ancient gate? Good. I see much of myself in your people, Cerim.
A faith of blood. A religion of war. We are what we kill.
A hunter has no right to protest when he becomes the hunted.
He was not wronged, only mistaken. He thought himself something other than prey.
Go, be the engine of their demise.
Carry nothing with you but ferocity.
Bloody your way to enlightenment.
Your eyes will betray you. Your ears will lie to you. Your blade will shatter.
Crutches, all of them.
Trust only in what you can feel, what you can strike.
For you were born with the only weapons you will ever need.
The bone breaks, the body heals, the will strengthens.
Your fist a hammer, your palm a thunderclap.
Make their death a work of art, an act of worship.
The weights around my crown, waist, and ankles urge me to stillness. When removed, they whisper me to war.
I cannot sense beyond your outline, Cerim. You are a void, a silhouette, a dark stain in the shape of a person.
Sacra is home to many peoples. Dasha, mainlanders, other isles, even the Far Lands. But violence is the one language we all speak.
A man of peace is a man at war.
Hone your one true weapon.
A sword's length is a coward's distance.
As God made us.
Your gifts - I do not need them. But I will take them.
You honor me, but this is not my temple. My altar lies out there, in the broken body of every foe.
You have more to learn. And now, thanks to your gift, I have more to teach.
I'm all for something that quickens your heartbeat, and God knows I'm fascinated by the varied and wondrous creatures of this world...
But I could do without the monstrosities that gate unleashed.
That's a curious fragrance you got about you. Ripe. ... Quite ripe.
Been tromping around where you don't belong? Start of any good adventure I suppose.
That a Balak Taw feather stuck to you? I've been practicing my own bird calls, maybe expand my customer base.
Think they'll let me in?
Never much cared for the Inquisition. Not the best conversationalists.
Though I am curious what lies beyond the Mountain Gate. My wife says I only ever want what I can't have.
I don't know what transpired in the Hunters' Vale, but I know how many hunters went out, and I know how few came back.
No no, it's alright, your secrets are your own. I'm your humble purveyor of goods, not your confidant. Not yet.
Ignore their gapes, Cerim, they've likely never seen one of your kind.
I, on the other hand, have met six Cerim. Five? Six? Many.
I've witnessed the seabirths of the Kylesh people to the south, and Arvos' northern cities that sail across the sands.
I once drank from the water pooled in a giant's footstep. And I've supped wine with Phalen's finest.
You and I, we're travelers.
Good to see you back, Cerim.
Been out exploring again?
I see you live to shop another day.
I must admit I've been waylaid on this humble island... longer than I'd like. But when the winds stall, the purse fills. Hmm, I should write that down.
See this scar? Pirate attack while crossing The Ashen Sea. Don't worry, we're all drinking friends now.
You know what they say about Giranoth women... down there? Well, it's not true.
Everything has a price! Every man has a cost!
I've scoured the realm so you don't have to!
The world at your fingertips!
I've got things you didn't know you couldn't live without!
Every trinket a treasure!
The greatest victory is a bargain!
Fresh wares delivered every morning!
I guarantee - shelves full again by sunrise!
Fantastic. I've enough shelves for every trinket now! Ehh, every invaluable piece of rare merchandise, is what I meant.
Look at what has become of my humble shop! I feel less a merchant, more a king. We live in an age of miracles, no?
I thank you, Cerim, but frankly this place is starting to look a bit too... permanent. Wanderlust has her teeth in me.
My thanks... ah, Cerim! A fellow walker of the planes.
My name is Finley. I traffic in the inconceivable, the unheard of, the unobtainable.
But my search for oddities led me... er, to this unenviable position. I am not a thief! Be quiet!
Now, in my untethered form, I shall return to Sacrament! You may see me there. But only when I want to be seen.
Yessss...! I can feel the wind of the world again…
You again... Thought you were still here.
Everything is for sale. Including myself perhaps.
Feast your eyes...
I came to Sacra from the west. Or maybe I'm heading west? Sometimes the arrow of time spins like a compass, wouldn't you say?
These penitent fools, always prattling on about the afterlife. What of the beforelife? The overlife? The underlife? Those matter too.
Settle a bet for us. For me, I mean. What would you say is the ideal number of me's and you's?
Who’s there? Someone… Of the flesh? Shhh! Be quiet. They’ll hear us.
You there! It is your - moral duty - to set me free! And me as well. How can you help, you don’t have hands!
Please. I’m a traveler like you. Of many realms. Spectral, astral, temporal.
But you must free me! Confinement of the body, of the bones inside the skin, it’s... It’s all wrong… Shut up! No one’s listening anyway.
Look at all this carnage. The dead becoming the living. The living the dead. How miraculous.
Which do you think came first?
Which one of you said that?
Enigmas for sale, paradoxes for purchase!
Buy now. Tomorrow one of us might be gone.
Shh, here they come… Ah, Cerim, the spectral warrior returns!
I told you I would be here, and here I am! Today at least. Tomorrow, I may be here yesterday.
I offer you my goods for a small fee, a trifle, a mere token of – I am not longwinded!
Only the heavens know what cause brings you to the Nameless Pass.
You have some fine trinkets on you... Yes, I see it!
I shall have to pass back by here in a few days’ time... you will make a very well-adorned corpse.
When you trade in wares as valuable as mine, never question their origin.
We like you, Cerim. You've become like a sister to us.
But if one of these monsters in the sky swoops down to feast on our flesh...
Well - I don't know if we could stay friends.
Yech! What a smell!
Didn't you hear, Mira? They've been down in the sewers!
Wish they would've stayed down there!
Say, we heard what you did for that village to the north.
We just want to say thank you. Not enough kindness shown to those poor Dasha.
They do some of the finest stitching on the island, they do. Almost as good as ours!
Been trotting around the Nameless Pass?
We heard you met the Madrigal!
Ooh, I'd love to get me hands on those fine robes of hers...
Did you hear Ellsworth's speech in the town square? Enough to make a lady swoon...
He's my future husband, you know.
Not if I snag him first!
Meri, have you heard - they say the Pestilence is in the Lowland Meadows now!
Dear me... Soon enough we'll have horrid things cropping up right here in Sacrament!
What, you mean like a person with two heads on one body? Imagine that!
Meriweather and Mirabelle - tailors at your service!
Meri, we agreed, my name goes first!
No no no, Mira, I remember we decided I go first!
Fine - we'll settle this later.
Looking a bit ragged I'd say - time for a change.
Worn yourself down to threads, you have.
About time you came back.
We were born behind these walls and we'll pass behind them.
They tell us Sacra's just a corner of the world, but it's our corner.
Can you tell one of us from the other, Cerim?
If so, you're better than our father!
Between the two of us we've got two husbands, eight children, and four chickens.
And they're all hers.
These are my scissors.
No, these are my scissors!
Shhh a customer!
Ms. Mider missed a spider on her scone now it's inside her.
Those rags you're wearing aren't fit for the fire.
Dear me, you look like a ball of yarn at the top of the stairs!
I'd say more like the bottom!
Snips and yarn, threads and cloth!
The only thing we hate's a moth!
Finally, a bit of room to breathe.
Some space to stretch out!
Many thanks, Cerim. You're not as bad as my sister says.
You were the one who said not to trust them!
Was I?
Could outfit a princess with these new tools!
Only Princess wandering into our stall is Grinnich's donkey.
Welcome young sprout. I go by Whittacker the Woodcrafter. That's because I craft wood.
Chipper and table are yours for the using. Or just leave the profession to the professional.
Hello again.
Let me know what you need.
So you're still on your feet.
If an oak takes a century to grow, least I can do is take my time in shaping what we make of it.
Tell you a secret - I don't work wood. I just listen to it. And it always tells me what it wants to be.
If I live to be a hundred, think someone'll make a chair out of me? Ha. Ha.
You cannot rush an oak.
Always go with the grain, young one.
Yew and pine, lose what's kind. Pine and yew, lose what's true.
From humble acorns, eh? Many thanks for the upgrade, Cerim.
I cannot wait to see what I can craft now. Well... I suppose I can always wait.
My stall has taken root. Its limbs reach for the sky. Apologies. I am not normally so giddy.
Keep walking, filth. I’ll trade no words with you.
These fools think they know who you are and where we’re headed, but they’ve got no idea.
You’ll be our doom, you will.
I fixed up your bed myself, real nice like.
Don’t fret if you can’t sleep - first few weeks aboard I couldn’t catch a wink.
Wort’s not what my ma named me. But, well, she’s gone now. And the men say I look more like a Wort anyway.
Cerim... Please... Help…
I tried to fight like you... But I can’t...
My name’s not Wort... It’s...
Captain wants a word with you up above!
Don’t mind the others. It’s just their way. You go speak with the Captain and I’ll check on your quarters.
Captain wants a word. He’s up on the bow.
You put the men on edge, Cerim. We’ve trafficked in people before but… Well. I won’t be sorry to be out of these waters with you off my ship.
I was paid to deliver you to Sacra in one piece. And I will.
But get to your quarters and stay out of our way until landfall. Wort will let you below decks.
Island’s just up ahead, through this damned storm. Get to your quarters. You’ll know you can come out when we stop moving.
Ey, you, a little help with the meal?
Fetch me the mushrooms from the shelf and herbs from the table. I have to keep stirring, or it’ll go from burned to ashes.
Just grab me that food.
In ya go. Along with a little seawater and a lot of sawdust hehe.
Sure, you can eat a mushroom in a pinch, but nothing beats a cooked meal. Here, have some for yourself.
I’d save it for gentler seas, else it’ll come up as fast as it goes down.
Not sure what you’re hopin’ to find on a shithole like Sacra.
Just Dasha families always one meal away from starvin’, and a buncha ruins that mean nothin’ to no one.
Sacra - the arsehole of the Empire.
Bad idea to let you on board...
That’s close enough! Just, just, keep your distance. There’s a dark about you, and I don’t want any part of it.
I... Please don’t hurt me.
No good will come of this...
Shoulda burned the island to the ground a thousand years ago and never come back.
We’ve wrecked and ravaged our way across half the Ashen Sea, and you’re scared of a hunk of rock?
I pray the Captain has the good sense to turn us around.
Never thought I’d see a Cerim warrior for myself.
I heard you were all seven feet tall, and big as oaks. Don’t look so tough to me.
Still, even I won’t set foot on Sacra. You’re a damned fool to go there.
Keep your eyes off our cargo ‘less you want one plucked out.
You’re too curious by half. Keep walking.
You ain’t the only thing we’re hauling. But at least the rest of our cargo stays where you put it.
If Cerim venture to Sacra, then the rumors must be true. The Pestilence has returned.
I don’t know whether you follow the sickness or it follows you, and I don’t care to know.
You keep your company, I’ll keep mine.
You’re just another job, far as I’m concerned.
The men think you’re some kind of legend. Know what all legends have in common? They’re dead.
Do me a favor, Cerim, and leave me out of your story.
I got it all planned out.
They’ll all be salutin’ me soon enough.
A year of this. Two of washing the decks. Four more in the rigging. Another five at the helm. And then captain! Just like that.
Perhaps a prayer before landfall?
Our ship might seem thick with sinners, but the Church welcomes all. Criminals, heretics. Even the Dasha. Even you.
Never too late to repent.
So you s’posed to be special or somethin’?
Leave ‘em be, Mers.
How ‘bout you lemme be a Cerim too? Bet that fancy cloak would look just fine on me.
You greedy bugger. You’d sell it sooner than save an infant.
Pfft, like they’re any different. They eat. They shit. They die. Same as the rest of us.
Oy, quit trying to edge your way in. Ain’t even enough for us.
Move along, Cerim.
Struttin’ about like you’re the only killer on board.
Difference between you and me? I don’t just kill sick people.
I mean… I would if there was any pay in it. Hehe.
Think the Silverfish would pay for the head of a Cerim?
A little space, eh? Not just the weather we have to contend with...
Plenty of mainland ships go missing off Sacra’s shores. We’re not the only ones on these waters.
Charting our way’s hard enough without you breathing down my neck.
